articles.title: Targeting the pyroptosis network: Research progress of natural products in intervention for acute lung injury.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a serious clinical condition with high morbidity and mortality rates. Current ALI treatments have limitations. Natural products from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exhibit multi-component, multi-target and multi-pathway regulatory properties with good safety, making them promising candidates for ALI treatment. This review systematically summarizes the activation pathways of pyroptosis, its molecular regulatory network in ALI and the mechanisms by which natural products regulate pyroptosis to inhibit ALI progression. A 'natural products-pyroptosis-ALI' axis conceptual framework is proposed to provide theoretical support for clinical translation. Systematic literature searches were conducted on CNKI, Web of Science and PubMed up to March 2026, using keywords related to natural products, ALI and pyroptosis. This review covers TCM herbs, natural small-molecule compounds and TCM formulas that modulate pyroptosis to alleviate ALI, with all animal experiments adhering to ethical and international standards. Various natural products and TCM formulae effectively target pyroptosis, inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, Caspase-1 activation and Gasdermin D pore formation, thereby reducing IL-1β/IL-18 release, alleviating inflammatory cascades, protecting alveolar-capillary barrier integrity and mitigating oxidative stress. Activated pyroptosis further disturbs mitophagy, triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, engages the gut-lung axis, modulates epigenetic reprogramming and promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition to amplify ALI. This review fills gaps in the systematic characterization of pyroptosis-ALI relationships and natural product-based therapies, aiming to expand ALI treatment options and advance ALI therapeutic development.

articles.title: Betel quid-induced oral carcinogenesis: emerging insights into genotoxicity, epigenetic aberration, and immune dysregulation.
articles.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a global health burden, particularly in South and Southeast Asia, where betel quid (BQ) chewing remains highly prevalent. As epidemiological evidence consistently identifies BQ as an independent risk factor for OSCC, recent high-throughput sequencing analyses and experimental mutagenesis studies have substantially advanced our understanding of the biological mechanisms underlying BQ-related oral tumorigenesis. This review provides an updated overview of the molecular and cellular alterations associated with chronic BQ exposure during OSCC development, with particular emphasis on genotoxicity, epigenetic and noncoding RNA-mediated remodeling, and immune dysregulation. BQ and its related constituents induce diverse forms of genomic instability in oral tissues, including chromosomal abnormalities, impaired DNA repair, characteristic mutational spectra/signatures, copy-number alterations, and loss of heterozygosity. Concurrently, chronic BQ exposure promotes widespread epigenetic dysregulation through altered DNA methylation, histone modification, and noncoding RNA-mediated pathways, resulting in silencing of tumor suppressor genes and activation of oncogenic signaling. Emerging evidence also suggests that BQ exposure may reshape the immune microenvironment of OSCC into a permissive niche for tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, highlighted by increased infiltration of tumor-associated macrophages, altered immunoregulatory dendritic cell programs, and activation of immune checkpoint pathways such as PD-L1/PD-1 and CD155/TIGIT. Collectively, these findings suggest that BQ-related OSCC may represent an etiologically defined subgroup of oral cancer with partially distinct genomic, epigenetic, and immunologic features, although further validation across anatomical sites, exposure patterns, and population backgrounds is required. A better understanding of these alterations may facilitate the development of novel prognostic biomarkers and precision therapeutic strategies for BQ-related oral cancer.

articles.title: Assessing the Risk of Neonatal Opioid Toxicity from Breastfeeding: Challenge to the Pediatric Clinical Pharmacology Modeling and Simulation Community.
articles.abstract: The safety of maternal codeine use during breastfeeding remains controversial, largely due to debate surrounding the "Toronto Case," in which a neonatal death was associated with elevated morphine exposure following maternal postpartum codeine therapy. Critics have argued that this outcome requires an exceptionally unlikely combination of several factors. This review details the physiological and pharmacokinetic complexities of infant opioid exposure and toxicity in breastfed infants by reexamining assumptions underlying the physiology-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model frequently cited to challenge the plausibility of the Toronto Case. When advances in developmental pharmacology, pharmacogenomics, and maternal and neonatal drug disposition that have occurred over the past 15 years are considered, an integrated mother-milk-infant system emerges in which individualized risk assessment can be conceptualized as the convergence of multiple factors, each of which contributes to the overall risk for a given mother-child dyad. Future modeling and simulations must include the maternal and neonatal determinants that predispose specific breastfeeding mother-newborn pairs to excessive sedation and respiratory failure after codeine administration, and generate evidence to support safer opioid therapy in breastfeeding mothers, breastfed infants, and older children.

articles.title: Smart nanofiber scaffolds for wound healing: Integrating biomimicry, drug delivery, and intelligent therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds still remain as one of the major clinical challenges, primarily because of persistent inflammation, microbial invasion, and compromised regenerative processes with conventional dressings offering largely passive protection with limited therapeutic benefit. Extracellular matrix (ECM)-mimicking biomaterials such as electrospun nanofiber, decellularized matrices and hydrogel based wound dressings represent a paradigm shift, offering ECM like architectures, high surface area and tunable physicochemical properties that enable modulation of cellular response and local wound microenvironment. This review highlights progress in nanofiber fabrication strategies, material innovations, and structure-function relationships, with emphasis on interactions between nanofibers and key cellular players including mesenchymal stem cells, fibroblasts, and keratinocytes. Beyond conventional drug delivery, we discuss hydrogel-integrated and dECM-functionalized nanofiber platforms for controlled therapeutic release, immune modulation, tissue repair, and physiologically relevant 3D disease modeling. We further examine the integration of biomarker-responsive elements and biosensing functionalities for real-time monitoring of wound status and controlled therapeutic release. The review also describes smart and adaptive wound systems, including stimuli-responsive nanofibers, closed-loop therapeutic platforms and the incorporation of emerging tools such as artificial intelligence and 3D/4D printing for adaptive, patient-specific nanofiber design. By moving beyond passive scaffolds towards dynamic, feedback regulated systems, this review outline a roadmap for next-generation programmable ECM-mimicking biomaterials with high clinical translation potential.

articles.title: Genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity switches: Molecular design, pharmacology, and therapeutic considerations.
articles.abstract: Genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity systems are chemogenetic tools that utilize small molecules to regulate protein association, higher-order assembly, and dissociation. Over the past three decades, an expanding repertoire of these systems has transformed the study of protein function and cellular signaling by enabling rapid, reversible, and tunable manipulation of protein localization, assembly, activity, and downstream physiological processes. As these technologies advance from experimental tools toward therapeutic applications, their translational potential depends not only on molecular switch performance but also on the properties of the chemical inducer and engineered protein components. In this review, we summarize the major classes and design principles of representative genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity systems, with particular emphasis on the pharmacological determinants that define their therapeutic operating window, including pharmacodynamic orthogonality, pharmacokinetics, tissue exposure, endogenous target engagement, and clinical readiness. We also examine how the biological origin and engineering of the chemogenetic modules influence immunogenicity and long-term compatibility. We further discuss exemplary applications, including pharmacological control of CAR-T cell activity, programmed cell death, CRISPR-based genome and epigenome engineering, and on-demand secretion of therapeutic proteins. Finally, we consider the delivery and coordinated expression of chemically regulated protein components as major remaining barriers to therapeutic implementation and highlight clinically compatible inducers, compact and minimally immunogenic protein modules, de novo protein design, and advances in viral and nonviral delivery as promising directions toward more reliable and pharmacologically tractable chemically controlled therapies.

articles.title: Prophages at the interface of antibiotic tolerance, persistence and antibiotic resistance: Evidence, mechanisms and therapeutic limits.
articles.abstract: Prophages are widespread in bacterial genomes, and several experimental systems show that they change how bacteria survive antibiotics. Using the consensus definitions of Balaban and colleagues, this review sorts the primary evidence by the endpoint actually measured: resistance defined by the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), tolerance (killing kinetics), persistence (biphasic killing), resuscitation (single-cell regrowth), and stress or biofilm survival. These endpoints are not treated as interchangeable. Effects depend on strain, prophage, antibiotic, and endpoint. In Escherichia coli, deleting nine cryptic prophages leaves persister formation unchanged but accelerates resuscitation. In Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, ciprofloxacin-induced Gifsy-1 lysis lowers persister survival, and TisB raises persister numbers largely by limiting that induction. In methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, φSA169 increases survival at a single 24 h vancomycin time point without changing the MIC, which is a survival difference at one time point and does not demonstrate tolerance or persistence. Unverified prophages can confound persistence assays. Prophage genomes rarely encode resistance genes; a Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical collection showed only infrequent prophage-resistance associations, and transduction can nonetheless move resistance determinants. Whether prophage-associated survival under antibiotic exposure promotes or restricts the evolution of resistance is an open hypothesis, supported by one species, one antibiotic, and a preprint, and a serial-passaging design to test it is outlined. Gut and probiotic prophages are abundant and inducible, but persistence data for them are lacking. Therapeutic approaches are separated into those acting on resident prophages, temperate phage-antibiotic synergy, and related but distinct strategies. Evidence that any prophage-directed intervention eliminates persisters in infection models is currently lacking. A minimum reporting checklist for future studies is provided.

articles.title: Metabolic Reprogramming in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Liver-Specific Immune Dysfunction, Immunotherapy Resistance, and Translational Biomarker Development.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arises in chronically injured, often fibrotic or cirrhotic liver, where metabolism, immunity, vascular and stromal organization, disease etiology, tumor state, and hepatic reserve are tightly interconnected. Although immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies have expanded treatment options for advanced HCC, responses remain heterogeneous because of both primary and acquired resistance. Metabolic reprogramming may shape these outcomes by altering nutrient availability, metabolite accumulation, antigen presentation, immune-cell fitness, stromal organization, and spatial immune access. This review provides an evidence-weighted assessment of major immunometabolic mechanisms in HCC, focusing on the glycolysis-hypoxia-lactate and tryptophan-kynurenine/IDO1 axes, lipid and cholesterol metabolism, purinergic signaling, mitochondrial and redox regulation, and ferroptosis. We emphasize that these pathways are context dependent, with effects determined by cellular source, differentiation state, spatial organization, and tumor-intrinsic versus immune-cell metabolic adaptation. Molecular heterogeneity, etiology, and cirrhosis are considered together, with WNT-β-catenin/CTNNB1-associated states illustrating their intersection with immune organization and ICI response. Because translational maturity varies widely, we distinguish mechanistic evidence, biomarker association, predictive validation, and clinical utility. We propose a framework integrating HCC specificity, primary human validation, cellular and spatial localization, causal immune-functional evidence, treatment-linked and longitudinal assessment, biomarker feasibility, and liver-specific safety. The framework also considers intervention timing and the distinction between primary and acquired ICI resistance. It may guide progression from metabolic discovery to spatially resolved mechanism, biomarker development, pharmacodynamic validation, and clinical evaluation while accounting for cirrhosis-associated remodeling, hepatic reserve, and treatment-related toxicity.

articles.title: Emerging strategies targeting the Hippo-YAP/TEAD pathway and the translational relevance in solid tumors.
articles.abstract: The Hippo-YAP/TEAD signaling axis regulates tissue growth, cellular identity, and organ homeostasis. Dysregulation of this pathway, through NF2 loss, LATS1 or LATS2 inactivation, or YAP1- or WWTR1-derived gene fusions, results in persistent nuclear localization of YAP/TAZ, driving TEAD-dependent transcriptional programs. NF2-deficient and YAP1/TAZ-driven tumors, such as mesothelioma, schwannoma, meningioma, and epithelioid hemangioendothelioma, exemplify Hippo-pathway dependency and are potential therapeutic targets. Targeting TEAD disrupts transcriptional circuits sustaining tumor growth, plasticity, and immune suppression while modulating metabolic and stromal dependencies. Pharmacologic interventions targeting YAP/TEAD include TEAD palmitate-binding pocket inhibitors, direct YAP/TEAD protein-protein interaction disruptors, PROTAC-mediated TEAD degraders, and YAP-directed antisense oligonucleotide strategies. Early-phase trials have demonstrated preliminary clinical activity, particularly with TEAD palmitate-binding pocket inhibitors in mesothelioma and have been associated with mild drug-related toxicities, such as proteinuria. YAP/TEAD inhibition may also be a rational combinatorial approach given the emergence of adaptive resistance mechanisms to EGFR/KRAS inhibitors and immunotherapies. Collectively, these findings provide rationale and early proof-of-concept for the pharmacologic targeting of the YAP/TEAD pathway. In this review, we describe the biological underpinnings of the YAP/TEAD pathway in cancer medicine, the anti-cancer strategies targeting this pathway, and discuss future directions in the field.

articles.title: Insulin Efsitora Alfa: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Insulin efsitora alfa (Onswik™) is a once-weekly ultra-long-acting recombinant basal insulin being developed by Eli Lilly and Company for the treatment of diabetes mellitus. Administered once weekly as a subcutaneous injection, insulin efsitora alfa is designed to provide a simplified treatment regimen relative to standard daily basal insulins. On 20 August 2026, insulin efsitora alfa received its first approval in the EU for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in adults. On 24 September 2026, insulin efsitora alfa was approved in the USA as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with T2DM. Insulin efsitora alfa is approved in the EU, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein and the USA and is under regulatory review in the UK and Japan for T2DM. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of insulin efsitora alfa leading to this first approval for T2DM.

articles.title: Daraxonrasib: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Daraxonrasib (RASONQUE™) is an oral, multiselective, noncovalent RAS(ON) inhibitor being developed by Revolution Medicines for the treatment of solid tumours, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), non-small-cell lung cancer and colorectal cancer. Daraxonrasib received its first approval in the USA on 26 August 2026 for the treatment of adults with metastatic PDAC who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of daraxonrasib leading to its first approval for metastatic PDAC.

articles.title: Oveporexton: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Oveporexton (ORZEYFULTM) is an oral selective orexin receptor 2 agonist developed by Takeda Pharmaceuticals Inc. for the treatment of narcolepsy type 1 (NT1). Oveporexton received its first approval in China on 22 July 2026 for the treatment of adolescents aged ≥ 16 years and adults with NT1. Subsequently, oveporexton was approved on 5 August 2026 in the USA and on 24 August 2026 in Japan for adults with NT1. Targeting the underlying orexin deficiency in NT1, oveporexton is the first and only agent approved for the treatment of NT1 addressing the full range of symptoms which define the condition. Additional global filings and phase III clinical trials are ongoing. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of oveporexton leading to this first approval for NT1.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of nonhormonal prescription drugs for vasomotor symptoms in women with breast cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vasomotor symptoms (VMS) are common during and after breast cancer treatment, particularly among women receiving endocrine therapy. We compared the efficacy, acceptability, and safety of nonhormonal prescription pharmacological interventions for VMS in women with breast cancer or breast cancer survivors. METHODS: We searched major databases and trial registries through July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing nonhormonal prescription drugs versus placebo or another eligible nonhormonal prescription drug in adult women with breast cancer-related VMS. The primary outcome was continuous VMS efficacy. Secondary outcomes included responder outcomes, all-cause discontinuation, discontinuation due to adverse events, any adverse events, and serious adverse events. We performed frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis, with Bayesian network meta-analysis as sensitivity analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence using a GRADE/NMA-GRADE approach. RESULTS: Eighteen publications, corresponding to 19 study/substudy records and 2,224 randomized or allocated participants, were included. Five interventions were significantly more effective than placebo: escitalopram (SMD -1.08, 95% CI -1.80 to -0.37), desvenlafaxine 50 mg (SMD -0.87, 95% CI -1.60 to -0.15), desvenlafaxine 100 mg (SMD -0.80, 95% CI -1.44 to -0.15), elinzanetant (SMD -0.51, 95% CI -0.95 to -0.07), and venlafaxine 75 mg (SMD -0.42, 95% CI -0.76 to -0.07). Heterogeneity was moderate (I2 = 44.9%), with no significant global or local inconsistency. Frequentist P-scores ranked the five significant drugs top, confirmed by Bayesian sensitivity. Elinzanetant had high-certainty evidence, whereas venlafaxine 75 mg and gabapentin 900 mg had moderate-certainty evidence. Escitalopram and desvenlafaxine had large effects, but the supporting evidence was sparse. Discontinuation outcomes showed no statistically significant differences versus placebo, but sparse safety networks precluded a reliable comparative safety hierarchy; these null findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent tolerability. CONCLUSION: Nonhormonal prescription drugs are not interchangeable for breast cancer-related VMS. Elinzanetant provides the strongest high-certainty evidence among newer targeted options, and venlafaxine 75 mg is the best-supported conventional option. Escitalopram and desvenlafaxine remain promising but require further trials. Gabapentin 900 mg may be considered in selected patients, whereas sertraline, bupropion, gabapentin 300 mg, and clonidine are lower-priority options. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261460108, identifier CRD420261460108.

articles.title: The targeted modulation of the inflammatory response to alleviate myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury via a biomimetic allicin delivery platform.
articles.abstract: Reperfusion strategies, the clinical standard for acute myocardial infarction, inevitably trigger severe myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (MI/R) injury. The acute phase of MI/R causes dual imbalance: excessive cardiomyocyte apoptosis and impaired macrophage phagocytosis. This pathological mechanism, the aberrant accumulation of apoptotic cells, triggers secondary necrosis, thereby serving as a critical driver of inflammatory storm and maladaptive cardiac remodeling. However, there is currently no targeted anti-inflammatory therapeutic strategy for this early pathological mechanism. To break these treatment limitations, we engineered a biomimetic stem cell membrane-camouflaged, allicin-loaded metal-organic framework nanoplatform (MOF-Al@NVs). Leveraging the nanovesicles' ischemic homing capability and the MOF's high drug-loading capacity and acidic degradation properties, this platform enables rapid, targeted delivery and release of allicin (which has anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory effects) within the ischemic myocardium. In vitro and in vivo investigations demonstrate that MOF-Al@NVs efficiently rescue dying cardiomyocytes by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) bursts and blocking the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. Concurrently, the platform re-orchestrates cardio-immune homeostasis by cooperatively upregulating the efferocytic receptor axis (TREM2/MERTK) on macrophages via activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade. This dual coordinative effect accelerates the clearance of cellular debris and promotes the anti-inflammatory phenotypic transition from M1 to M2 macrophages, thereby attenuating the inflammatory storm, ameliorating acute-phase MI/R-induced cardiac dysfunction, and improving short-term prognosis. High-resolution spatial transcriptomics, integrated with multi-omics, confirms that MOF-Al@NVs effectively restore spatial immunometabolic homeostasis in the early infarct border zone. This biomimetic nanoplatform offers a promising strategy for targeted anti-inflammatory therapy in early MI/R injury.

articles.title: Silk fibroin-functionalized nanoemulsion for prolonged corneal retention and mitochondrial protection in dry eye.
articles.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a prevalent ocular surface disorder that can progress to corneal epithelial damage and, in severe cases, vision loss. Effective management of DED is hampered by unfavorable physicochemical properties of both the ocular surface barrier and drug molecules. Resveratrol (RSV) exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities but is limited by poor aqueous solubility and low ocular bioavailability. In this study, we formulated an RSV-loaded oil-in-water nanoemulsion eye drops (RSV-SF-NEs) with silk fibroin (SF) as a multifunctional core component. SF is a natural protein that serves simultaneously as an effective emulsifier to stabilize the nanoemulsion interface, a mucin-1 (MUC1)-targeted adhesion ligand to prolong corneal retention, and an intrinsic antioxidant to synergistically scavenge free radicals. SF's multifunctionality enabled a 3-fold increase in ocular surface retention over free DiR and enhanced corneal epithelial uptake of RSV. In vitro, RSV-SF-NEs were internalized by corneal epithelial cells via macropinocytosis and protected cells from injury by inhibiting oxidative stress and restoring mitochondrial homeostasis. In a benzalkonium chloride-induced mouse dry eye model, RSV-SF-NEs reduced ocular surface inflammation and oxidative stress, accelerated corneal epithelial repair, and restored tear secretion. RSV-SF-NEs showed superior efficacy to cyclosporine A (CsA) eye drops and exhibited no obvious toxicity. Corneal proteomics revealed that RSV-SF-NEs exerted therapeutic effects by reversing dysregulated expression of mitochondrial proteins involved in oxidative phosphorylation and energy metabolism. This SF-centered "vector-function" strategy offers a promising therapeutic approach for DED.

articles.title: A Th17-centered immune network for tertiary lymphoid structure formation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT) benefits esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), yet underlying antitumor immunity remains elusive. This study aimed to dissect the cellular and molecular determinants and identify predictive biomarkers of NICT response in ESCC. METHODS: Longitudinal single-cell RNA and T/B cell receptor sequencing was performed on paired pre- and post-NICT ESCC samples from 20 patients. Spatial analyses and functional assays were employed to investigate the compartmentalized distribution and functional adaptation of cells within ESCC tumor microenvironment in response to NICT. RESULTS: Through single-cell multi-omics profiling of ESCC tumors, we identified Th17 accumulation accompanied by IL-22 and IL-17A upregulation in responders after NICT. IL-22 promoted differentiation of IL22RA1+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) into CCL19+ CAFs and tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) formation. Th17-derived IL-17A primed B cells differentiation toward the TNFSF9+ B trajectory with increased antibody production. Pretreatment quantification of IL22RA1⁺ fibroblasts predicted NICT response in ESCC. In mice, hydroxycholesterols or IL-17A and IL-22 supplementation induced TLS formation and improved immunochemotherapy efficacy. CONCLUSIONS: Our work delineates a Th17-CAF-B cell axis critical for TLS neogenesis and NICT response in ESCC, providing mechanism-based biomarkers for patient stratification and strategies to overcome treatment resistance.

articles.title: AKR1B1-dependent ferroptosis defense contributes to KRASG12C inhibitor resistance in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: AIMS: To investigate the role of AKR1B1-associated ferroptosis defense in acquired KRASG12Cinhibitor (G12Ci) resistance in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells, and to evaluate the antitumor activity of AKR1B1 inhibition combined with KRASG12C inhibition in xenograft models. METHODS: Sotorasib- and adagrasib-resistant PDAC cell populations were analyzed using integrated genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and phosphoproteomic profiling. The functional roles of AKR1B1 and YAP1 were assessed using siRNA-mediated knockdown, ferroptosis-rescue assays, and pharmacological inhibition with epalrestat. The combination of epalrestat and sotorasib was also evaluated in treatment-naïve cell line-derived and patient-derived xenograft models. RESULTS: Multi-omics profiling identified AKR1B1 upregulation in sotorasib- and adagrasib-resistant MIA PaCa-2 cells. In these in vitro resistant cell models, AKR1B1 knockdown reduced YAP1 and SLC7A11 expression and cystine uptake, while increasing lipid peroxidation. Epalrestat enhanced the growth-inhibitory effects of G12Ci in resistant cells, with localized synergy at selected concentrations. In treatment-naive MIA PaCa-2 CDX, KRASG12C-mutant PDX, and UMUC3 CDX models, epalrestat plus sotorasib suppressed tumor growth more than either agent alone. CONCLUSIONS: AKR1B1-associated ferroptosis defense contributes to acquired KRAS G12Ci resistance in PDAC cell models, and AKR1B1 inhibition enhances sotorasib activity in treatment-naive xenograft models. These findings support further evaluation of AKR1B1 inhibition as a combination strategy for KRASG12Cmutant PDAC.

articles.title: One Health genomic surveillance reveals transmission networks, resistance profiles and dissemination patterns of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Genomic connectivity of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) across clinical-environmental interfaces remains poorly characterised. We investigated these relationships through hospital-centred One Health surveillance. METHODS: Prospective, year-long surveillance across five Chinese provinces yielded 298 environmental A. baumannii isolates from 3148 non-clinical samples, analysed alongside 436 clinical isolates. We integrated phylogenetics, lineage-specific core-genome single-nucleotide polymorphism (cgSNP) networks and epidemiological records. Based on a separate genome-similarity clustering scheme, genome-environment models estimated relative cluster dominance within hospital-season samples (ITI) and predicted same-hospital cluster re-detection the following season (fITI). RESULTS: Lineage-specific analyses across five dominant sequence types identified 55 genomic clusters at a ≤ 10-cgSNP threshold. Genomic links were predominantly intraprovincial (92.7%), with interprovincial and cross-setting connections. Epidemiological and temporal evidence supported 116 putative transmission-associated genomic links, including 19 air-associated links between environmental isolates. Air-derived isolates occurred in 12 local genomic subnetworks across hospital and non-hospital settings. Retrospective evaluation yielded mean leave-one-province-out areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.925 for conditional pairwise ITI discrimination and 0.711 for fITI classification. Corresponding values in independent historical validation were 0.861 and 0.714. CONCLUSIONS: These findings place hospital-centred CRAB circulation in a broader ecological context and support genomic surveillance incorporating air sampling, alongside models to assess cluster dominance and predict re-detection.

articles.title: PAR2-TRPV4 functional interaction drives epithelial barrier dysfunction through a protein kinase C epsilon (PKCε)-Ca2+ feedback loop in house dust mite-induced allergic rhinitis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Allergic rhinitis involves epithelial barrier dysfunction that current therapies address poorly, especially in house dust mite (HDM) allergy. We hypothesized that HDM allergens up-regulate protease-activated receptor 2 (PAR2) and transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) in nasal epithelium and that these receptors functionally interact to regulate tight junction (TJ) integrity through calcium-dependent protein kinase C (PKC) signalling. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Nasal mucosa and brush cells from 30 allergic rhinitis patients and 30 controls (10 HDM-sensitized) were examined by quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), immunostaining and western blotting. A Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus group 1 allergen (Der p 1)-induced epithelial model enabled synergy analysis, calcium imaging, site-directed mutagenesis and genetic manipulation, with transepithelial electrical resistance as readout. Ovalbumin (OVA)- and HDM-induced mouse models and PAR2/TRPV4 antagonists were evaluated. KEY RESULTS: In HDM-allergic patients, PAR2 was up-regulated and TRPV4 showed epithelium-specific up-regulation, and in this exploratory pilot subgroup, PAR2 correlated with claudin-1 and ZO-1. Synergy analysis showed that TRPV4 inhibition blocked PAR2-mediated barrier disruption, whereas co-activation was only weakly synergistic. We identified a PKCε-Ca2+-TRPV4 positive feedback loop, in which PAR2 activation engages PKCε signalling and requires the N-terminal tyrosine Y110 of TRPV4 for sustained calcium influx that amplifies TJ disassembly. PAR2 and TRPV4 up-regulation occurred in HDM- but not OVA-induced disease. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Inhibition of PAR2 or TRPV4 restored epithelial barrier function in HDM-induced allergic rhinitis, with dual antagonism most effective. These findings identify PAR2 and TRPV4 as barrier-protective therapeutic targets, complementary to existing anti-inflammatory treatment.

articles.title: Oxidative stress and genetic susceptibility to cross-reactive and selective NSAID hypersensitivity.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are a leading cause of drug hypersensitivity reactions (HRs), but genetic determinants of individual susceptibility remain unclear. Here, we identified genetic variants in redox- and immune-related pathways associated with cross-reactive NSAID hypersensitivity (CR-NSAID) and single-NSAID-induced urticaria/angioedema/anaphylaxis (SNIUAA) and to characterize their functional relevance. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: A multicentre prospective case-control study was conducted in Spanish individuals of European ancestry, including patients with confirmed NSAID hypersensitivity and NSAID-tolerant individuals. Single nucleotide variants (SNVs) in redox- and immune-related genes were genotyped using a two-stage discovery and independent replication design. SNVs showing significant associations were functionally evaluated by measuring serum glutathione S-transferase (GST), superoxide dismutase (SOD) and aldo-keto reductase (AKR) activities according to genotype. KEY RESULTS: GSTM5 rs11101989 and GSTZ1 haplotype (rs1046428, rs7975, rs7972) associated with increased susceptibility to CR-NSAID. Functional analyses demonstrated that carriers of the GSTM5 rs11101989 CC genotype had significantly reduced total serum GST activity. In SNIUAA, SOD1 variants (rs2070424 and rs2833483) associated with increased susceptibility and reduced serum SOD activity. Additionally, AKR1C3 rs34186955 increased susceptibility, whereas AKR1C3 rs12529 and IL4R rs1805016 associated with decreased susceptibility. Integration of genetic and functional data supported involvement of redox-related pathways in distinct NSAID hypersensitivity phenotypes and identified GSTM5 and SOD1 variants as candidate genetic susceptibility markers. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Genetic variability in redox-related and immune-regulatory pathways contributed to susceptibility to cross-reactive and selective NSAID hypersensitivity. These findings support further validation of biomarker-based strategies for personalized risk assessment and safer NSAID prescribing. Further validation in independent populations is required.

articles.title: Sex-specific effects of prenatal vitamin D supplementation on repetitive behaviour and neuroimmune mediators in the BTBR mouse model of autism spectrum disorders.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are prevalent in males compared with females, possibly attributed to male-centric profiles diagnostic criteria. ASD pathogenesis involves neuroinflammation and altered immune signalling. Therefore, maternal vitamin D deficiency may contribute to ASD by impairing fetal neurodevelopment, promoting immune dysregulation and inflammatory conditions. Due to the difficult recruitment of the vulnerable paediatric population, we used BTBR T + tf/J (BTBR) male and female mice, characterized by core ASD-like behaviours, to investigate the effects of prenatal vitamin D supplementation. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: On gestational day 9, pregnant BTBR dams received a subcutaneous injection of either vitamin D3 (400 ng·kg-1) or vehicle. At 8-week-old, offspring underwent a battery of behavioural tests, including Hole Board, Marble Burying, Self-grooming, Open Field and Social Interaction tests. mRNA expression and protein levels of tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), transforming growth factor-β2 (TGF-β2), fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) and resistin in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus were then quantified. KEY RESULTS: Maternal vitamin D supplementation reduced BTBR stereotypies. Moreover, vitamin D decreased cortical and hippocampal protein TNF-α levels only in BTBR males. In addition, vitamin D upregulated hippocampal TGF-β2 gene expression and FABP4 gene expression and protein content in male offspring, whereas a down-regulation of TGF-β2 mRNA and protein levels was reported in females. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Our findings indicated that prenatal vitamin D supplementation exerted beneficial effects on BTBR stereotypies, neuroinflammatory and neuroimmune signalling alterations, ultimately suggesting its potential as an early preventive strategy to target ASD sex-tailored biomolecular dysfunctions.

articles.title: ImmunoPET-guided TIM-3 theranostics enables dynamic visualization of adaptive immune escape and targeted radioimmunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Suboptimal responses and adaptive resistance remain major hurdles to immunotherapy, necessitating noninvasive dynamic in vivo monitoring of emerging immune checkpoints and the subsequent development of targeted interventions. TIM-3 is closely associated with T-cell exhaustion and immunotherapy resistance. Nevertheless, no remarkable breakthroughs have been achieved in TIM-3-targeted therapeutic strategies. Here, we report a first-in-class TIM-3-targeted radio-theranostic platform based on the humanized anti-TIM-3 antibody T21(TQB2618), radiolabeled with 89Zr (zirconium-89) for immunoPET imaging and 177Lu (lutetium-177) for radionuclide therapy. 89Zr-T21 exhibited high TIM-3 affinity and target specificity at protein and cellular levels and enabled clear visualization of TIM-3-positive expression tumors. In a hTIM-3 humanized animal model, 89Zr-T21 initially showed dominant splenic uptake and limited tumor accumulation, consistent with a peripheral TIM-3 antigen sink, whereby abundant TIM-3-expressing immune cells sequester the tracer outside the tumor. Pre-administration of unlabeled T21 reduced splenic sequestration and optimized tumor visualization, with maximal tumor uptake achieved at a 25-fold pre-dosing level. Notably, 89Zr-T21 enabled longitudinal and noninvasive monitoring of immunotherapy-induced TIM-3 remodeling in vivo, revealing time-dependent TIM-3 upregulation following PD-1 blockade and dose-dependent TIM-3 expression changes after immunotherapy. The matched therapeutic agent 177Lu-T21 significantly inhibited A549hTIM-3 tumor growth with favorable safety. Collectively, this study establishes the first TIM-3-directed radio-theranostic framework for imaging adaptive immune resistance and advancing TIM-3 targeted radioimmunotherapy.

articles.title: Graph learning guided by regulatory and spatial contexts prioritizes natural compound-target pairs in digestive system cancers.
articles.abstract: Heterogeneity in tumor regulatory programs, cellular composition and spatial organization complicates target prioritization for natural compounds. We developed a spatial-context heterogeneous graph neural network ranker (SC-HGNN-Rank) that combines relation-aware graph representations with ranking optimization to integrate compound-target associations, transcriptional regulation, interaction networks, and single-cell and spatial information. The model ranked 600 candidate axes in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD), hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) and gastric adenocarcinoma (STAD). Under matched training conditions, mean Spearman correlations with the reference ranking were 0.965, 0.967 and 0.976 for leave-one-cancer-out, compound-group holdout and target-group holdout evaluations, respectively. The composite ranking objective improved mean Spearman correlation by 0.049 over a simple objective using the same encoder, whereas removing the spatial module reduced it by 0.147. Model ranking and multilayer evidence prioritized Quercetin-CDK1/MYB-Myeloid in COAD, 4',5-dihydroxyflavone (4',5-DHF)-AR/HDAC1-T/NK in LIHC, and Eriodyctiol-HSP90AB1/HOPX-Fibroblast in STAD. Expanded spatial analyses with expression-matched gene controls assessed associations between target expression and mapped cell abundance. Cellular thermal shift and drug affinity responsive target stability assays showed increased retention of target proteins after compound treatment. In HCT116, JHH-6 and MKN45 cells, the compounds reduced viability, colony formation, migration and invasion cell counts, and increased apoptosis. Target knockdown produced similar growth-inhibitory phenotypes, whereas overexpression attenuated compound-induced effects, supporting the involvement of CDK1, AR and HSP90AB1 in the respective responses. The accompanying Explorer supports candidate searches, evidence inspection and data export. By incorporating regulatory and spatial contexts into natural-compound prioritization, this study provides a reusable approach and experimentally supported candidates for target-directed pharmacological research in digestive system cancers.

articles.title: An aptamer/hydrogel system for prolonged sustained drug delivery.
articles.abstract: Prolonged drug effect from a single-dose administration offers therapeutic advantages. To achieve that goal, we developed a hydrogel modified with an aptamer to a specific drug (Gel-Apt). This system, using both affinity- and diffusion-controlled mechanisms allowed increased duration of effect and decreased systemic toxicity. We demonstrate the efficacy of this system with tetrodotoxin (TTX), an ultrapotent local anesthetic, in rat sciatic nerve block. Gel-Apt loaded with TTX caused nerve block lasting 39 h. This system using both affinity-and diffusion-controlled mechanisms could be applicable to any drug for which there is a specific aptamer.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal coordination of a bacteria-targeted ultrasound-light cascade for synergistic eradication of MRSA biofilm-associated infections.
articles.abstract: Restricted delivery of antimicrobial agents into biofilms limits the treatment of implant-associated infections. Here, we developed UBI₂₉-₄₁-functionalized lipid nanobubbles co-loaded with vancomycin (Van) and an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) photosensitizer (UBI-Van/AIE@NBs) for sequential ultrasound (US)-assisted and photodynamic treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) biofilms. The formulation exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 480.3 ± 40.8 nm and a positive zeta potential. US increased cumulative Van and AIE release to approximately 82% and 74%, respectively, within 5 min, compared with 27-28% without US. Cell-free probe assays supported AIE-associated reactive oxygen species generation during white-light irradiation. Fluorescence imaging suggested enhanced biofilm association and prolonged signal retention at the infection site. In vitro, sequential US and light exposure reduced residual biofilm biomass and viable bacterial counts more effectively than either stimulus alone, with UBI-Van/AIE@NBs producing the lowest residual biomass and bacterial recovery under combined treatment. In a murine titanium implant-associated MRSA infection model, the combined regimen reduced implant-associated bacterial burden and accelerated wound closure, accompanied by reduced inflammation, improved collagen organization, and increased CD31 staining. The formulation exhibited low cytotoxicity and hemolysis, without apparent major-organ injury or significant changes in serum biochemical parameters under the tested conditions. These findings support integrating peptide functionalization, US-enhanced cargo release, and photodynamic treatment as a preclinical strategy for localized management of implant-associated MRSA biofilm infections.

articles.title: Acipimox as a clinical pharmacology probe: A two-level bibliometric analysis of antilipolysis and bioenergetic readouts.
articles.abstract: Acipimox was introduced as a nicotinic acid analogue for lipid modification, but its later use has shifted towards experimental suppression of lipolysis in human metabolic studies. We examined whether this pattern reflects loss of drug identity or mechanism-constrained reuse of an established pharmacodynamic effect. Bibliographic records from PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus were harmonized into a frozen dataset of 863 records. A nested two-level framework defined a Broad Application Space (n = 428), within which a stricter Drug-Identity Core (n = 239) was identified. Bibliometric mapping was interpreted alongside landmark pharmacological studies to preserve a clinical pharmacology perspective. The 428-record Broad Application Space comprised 239 Drug-Identity Core records and 189 Broad-only application/probe records. The nested Core remained centred on lipid lowering, tolerability, lipolytic-enzyme regulation and suppression of free fatty acid availability, whereas the additional Broad-only literature extended into insulin sensitivity, endocrine physiology, skeletal-muscle fuel handling and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide- and mitochondrial-linked metabolic readouts. The pivotal pharmacological signal was not a complete transformation of acipimox into a mitochondrial drug, but recurrent experimental reuse of receptor-linked antilipolysis. Acipimox illustrates how an older compound can retain value when a well-characterized pharmacodynamic action is reused as a probe of lipid substrate availability, substrate competition and selected bioenergetic readouts. Such use requires explicit attention to timing, rebound non-esterified fatty acids and tissue context.

articles.title: Bioequivalence of two formulations of amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The study evaluated the bioequivalence and tolerability of a generic amitriptyline hydrochloride tablet compared to the reference product in healthy Chinese subjects under both fasting and postprandial conditions to support its marketing authorization. METHODS: A single-center, open-label, randomized, single-dose, two-period, two-sequence crossover study was conducted. Eligible subjects took a single 25 mg dose of the generic or reference product per cycle in random order. Plasma drug concentrations were detected by LC-MS/MS and the bioequivalence of the two formulations was assessed through key pharmacokinetic parameters (Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-∞) of amitriptyline. Adverse events were continuously monitored throughout the trial. RESULTS: The 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for the geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-∞ between the two products fell within the 80-125% range under both fasting and postprandial conditions. Our study indicated that food intake increases systemic exposure to amitriptyline without affecting Tmax. Both formulations were well tolerated, with predominantly mild adverse events and no severe or fatal events. CONCLUSION: The generic amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets by Changzhou Siyao Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. were bioequivalent to the reference formulation by Sandoz Inc. with comparable tolerability. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered at www.chinadrugtrials.org.cn under the registration number CTR20212242 (November 2, 2021).

articles.title: Artificial intelligence support for the prediction and management of drug-drug interactions.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) are a preventable cause of adverse drug events (ADEs), yet conventional interaction-checking tools are hampered by incomplete knowledge, poor concordance, and clinically unusable alert burdens. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly utilized to strengthen multiple stages of the DDI pathway. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review synthesizes literature identified through searches conducted between 15 July and 20 October 2026. It examines how machine learning (ML) predicts novel drug interactions from molecular structure and knowledge graphs; how natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs) identify and extract interactions from the literature, drug labels, and pharmacovigilance data; and how AI can make clinical decision support context-aware and support medication review. It also integrates mechanistic physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling and individualized patient-level risk prediction. EXPERT OPINION: Prediction models achieve impressive benchmark accuracy but frequently underperform in realistic, cold-start settings; LLMs detect interactions with high sensitivity but show poor severity calibration and persistent hallucination. The near-term value of AI lies less in autonomous prediction than in curating knowledge, personalizing alerts, and augmenting clinician judgment. Rigorous external validation, interpretability, and regulatory clarity are prerequisites for clinical adoption.

articles.title: Huanglian Jiedu Decoction: An Ethnopharmacological Perspective on Molecular Mechanisms and Clinical Applications in Inflammatory Diseases.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Huanglian Jiedu Decoction (HLJDD) is a classic traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) renowned for its heat-clearing and detoxifying effects. For centuries, this formula has been widely used under the guidance of TCM theory to treat various inflammatory disorders characterized as "heat toxin" or "excess fire in the three burners." TCM considers "heat toxin" to be a common pathological mechanism underlying many inflammatory diseases, with clinical manifestations functionally analogous and corresponding to the infectious and non-infectious inflammation defined by modern Western medicine, rather than being strictly equivalent. Therefore, the traditional effects of HLJDD in clearing heat, purging fire, detoxifying, and cooling the blood provide a unique TCM theoretical foundation and alternative intervention strategy for the treatment of modern inflammatory diseases. AIM OF THE REVIEW: This review aims to systematically summarize the components, traditional efficacy, main active ingredients of HLJDD in inflammatory diseases, as well as its modern pharmacological effects and molecular mechanisms. By integrating traditional experience with modern scientific evidence, we strive to provide a solid scientific basis and translational strategies for the ethnomedicinal applications of this herbal medicine and its modern use in the prevention and treatment of inflammatory diseases. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative literature search was performed in PubMed and CNKI from database inception to December 31, 2025, using "Huanglian Jiedu Decoction", "HLJDD", "anti-inflammatory", "inflammation" and their synonyms. Original research articles on the phytochemistry, network pharmacology, mechanisms, or clinical applications of HLJDD or its constituent herbs in inflammatory diseases were included; reviews, case reports, non-English/Chinese publications, and duplicates were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts, with disagreements resolved by consensus. A three-tier evidence classification (whole formula / single herb / pure compound) was applied to mechanistic studies, and findings were synthesized narratively given substantial heterogeneity. Only PubMed and CNKI were searched, which may limit comprehensiveness. RESULTS: The anti-inflammatory activity of HLJDD is mainly attributed to its various alkaloids and flavonoid compounds. These components exert synergistic effects through multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms, significantly inhibiting the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines (such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) and effectively regulating the activation of key inflammatory signaling pathways (such as NF-κB, MAPK, JAK-STAT, and the NLRP3 inflammasome). Both in vivo and in vitro experiments have confirmed that HLJDD exhibits significant anti-inflammatory and tissue-protective effects in various inflammatory disease models, including sepsis, acute lung injury, colitis, and skin inflammation. Its mechanism of action is characterized by a typical "multi-component, multi-target, multi-pathway" network regulation feature. CONCLUSIONS: What is established is that HLJDD and its constituent compounds modulate the NF-κB, MAPK, JAK-STAT, and NLRP3 pathways in cellular and animal systems, although most mechanistic evidence derives from isolated compounds rather than the whole formula. What is suggestive is that HLJDD-containing interventions may confer clinical benefit in selected inflammatory conditions; however, current clinical evidence remains of very low certainty, as most reported studies are small-sample, non-blinded trials using modified formulas or combination therapies rather than the classic HLJDD formula alone. What remains hypothetical is whether these preclinical mechanisms translate into clinically meaningful efficacy in humans. Future research should therefore prioritize: in-depth mechanistic studies that rigorously distinguish whole-formula from compound-level evidence; standardized extraction and quality-control systems; delivery systems to improve bioavailability; and large-scale, rigorously designed randomized controlled trials-so that HLJDD may progressively advance from empirical use toward a safe and effective evidence-based anti-inflammatory therapy..

articles.title: Buforin IIb in Antimicrobial and Anticancer Pharmacology; Crossing Membranes, Crossing Therapeutic Boundaries.
articles.abstract: Buforin IIb is a 21-residue antimicrobial peptide rationally engineered from buforin II, which itself derives from the histone H2A-derived gastric peptide buforin I. Unlike many cationic host-defence peptides that kill primarily through membrane permeabilization, buforin IIb can cross microbial and cancer-cell membranes with limited lytic disruption and engage intracellular targets, including nucleic acids and organelles. These properties support its broad antimicrobial activity and preferential cytotoxicity toward multiple malignant cell lines. This review traces the structural determinants of this activity, principally a helix-hinge-helix architecture organized around a single proline residue and examines the mechanistic evidence for ganglioside-mediated cancer-cell recognition, mitochondria- and endoplasmic-reticulum-associated apoptotic signalling, reported p53-associated responses, cell-cycle arrest, and ARF6-associated immunogenic cell death. It also examines pharmaceutical engineering strategies developed to address the peptide's principal limitations, including limited in vivo stability, incomplete cancer selectivity, and hemolytic activity at high concentrations. These strategies include matrix metalloproteinase-activatable prodrugs, BR2-based delivery systems, nanoparticle and metal bioconjugates, N-terminal lipidation, and tumour-responsive combination nanomedicines. The review synthesizes evidence from primary experimental studies describing the structural determinants, pharmacological activities, and therapeutic engineering of buforin IIb. Finally, it critically examines the major translational challenges that continue to limit its clinical development, including stability, selectivity, pharmacokinetics, and scalable manufacturing.

articles.title: Repurposing drugs for aortic aneurysm: unlocking new therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease for which no pharmacological therapy has been proven to effectively limit disease progression. Drug repurposing (DR), which leverages existing drugs with established safety profiles, offers a promising and cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic development for AA. In this review, we summarize recent advances in DR research for AA, highlighting the emerging framework that integrates computational prediction with experimental and clinical validation. We discuss key repurposed drug candidates, evaluate the current state of translational evidence, and examine the challenges that have hindered clinical success despite encouraging preclinical findings. Finally, we outline opportunities to enhance target identification, patient stratification, and clinical trial design. By bridging mechanistic discovery and translational application, DR may provide a practical pathway toward effective medical therapies for aneurysmal disease.

articles.title: Fit-for-purpose identification of degradation products in hospital compounding: grading confidence with combined LC-HRMSⁿ and DFT.
articles.abstract: Hospital pharmacists increasingly prepare oral liquid formulations from commercially available tablets and capsules for patients unable to swallow solid dosage forms. These reformulations modify the physicochemical environment of the drug substance, so published stability data are not always directly applicable to the compounded preparation. Although experimental stability studies remain essential, they cannot cover every formulation used in hospital practice. Mechanistic studies can help interpret degradation behaviour under these new conditions. High-resolution mass spectrometry, combined with density functional theory, can identify plausible degradation pathways, support analytical method development and help design targeted stability studies. Their purpose is not to replace experimental stability studies, which remain necessary to establish the stability of a preparation, but to help target them. While this analytical combination is established, we propose to report degradation products using explicit, ordinal levels of identification confidence, adapted from metabolomics and non-target analysis, in which diagnostic fragmentation and converging computational evidence may support a probable structure without an authentic standard. We further suggest, as a fit-for-purpose principle rather than a regulatory requirement, that the level sought be matched to the pharmaceutical question being addressed. This approach could improve the interpretation of degradation studies and the transferability of mechanistic knowledge in hospital compounding.

articles.title: Physical energy-assisted drug delivery systems: mechanistic study of intracellular delivery enhancement and off-target reduction.
articles.abstract: For many therapeutics the limiting step is delivery, not target identification. Macromolecules and charged small molecules often fail to reach the cytosol or nucleus at therapeutic concentrations, and the higher systemic doses used to compensate bring their own off-target toxicity. Physical energy-assisted drug delivery systems (PE-DDS) address this by adding an orthogonal control variable, an externally applied input such as ultrasound, an electric or magnetic field, light, heat, or mechanical force, used to modulate biological barriers and carrier behavior with spatial and temporal precision. This review analyzes PE-DDS through two linked questions: how physical energy enhances intracellular delivery, and how the same inputs reduce exposure of healthy tissue. We included studies in which energy regulated transport, uptake, trafficking, or localized release, and excluded those in which it acted as a cytotoxic effector without a defined delivery function. We graded evidence on three tiers by the endpoint each study measured: Demonstrated, Inferred, and Enabling. Delivery was resolved into four levels: cellular association, internalization, endosomal escape, and functional delivery. Applying these criteria, functional delivery is measured mainly in ex vivo and in vitro systems, and direct measurement of reduced non-target exposure remains rare. Because no single modality fits every setting, the choice must match tissue depth, the relevant biological barrier, cargo properties, and the therapeutic safety window. Standardized energy dosimetry and routine inclusion of non-target endpoints are now the limiting requirements for translation.

articles.title: Engineering mRNA lipid nanoparticle for protein replacement in rare genetic diseases - current advances and future challenges.
articles.abstract: Rare genetic diseases affect over 350 million patients worldwide and have long posed significant challenges in modern medicine. Although messenger RNA (mRNA) was initially considered unsuitable due to its instability, immunogenicity, and inability to cross biological barriers, the COVID-19 pandemic established mRNA as a clinically validated therapeutic. Advances in mRNA synthesis and lipid nanoparticle (LNP) design have since improved stability, translation, safety, and scalability, offering a modern strategy, alongside advances in our understanding of rare diseases. By enabling the production of functional proteins without modifying the genome, mRNA-LNP offer a flexible solution to restore proteins lost through rare genetic diseases. Despite this promise, their application for rare genetic diseases remains at early stages, with most candidates in preclinical developments or early Phase 1/2 trials. This review underlines recent advances in mRNA-based protein replacement for rare genetic disorders, integrating innovations in mRNA design combined with LNPs optimization. It also discusses current challenges, emerging innovations, and future perspectives. While early clinical programs have mainly targeted liver-based disorders, the field is expanding toward pulmonary, hematologic, and neuromuscular diseases. Continued multidisciplinary efforts may establish mRNA nanotherapies as a transformative treatment option for patients with rare genetic disorders.

articles.title: Endothelial SULF1 in cardiovascular disease: Structural basis of heparan sulfate editing and context-dependent pharmacology.
articles.abstract: Heparan sulfate 6-O-endosulfatase 1 (SULF1) is an extracellular enzyme that edits mature heparan sulfate and thereby influences the binding and availability of extracellular signaling molecules. We focus on the role of endothelial SULF1 in cardiovascular disease. We also summarize its main structural domains, extracellular processing, catalytic features, and substrate recognition. Then we discuss how SULF1 affects heparan sulfate-dependent signaling, with particular attention to fibroblast growth factor (FGF), vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A), and Wnt pathways. Available evidence suggests that the effects of SULF1 vary across disease settings. After myocardial infarction, SULF1 may promote vascular repair by increasing the availability of matrix-bound VEGF-A. In atherosclerosis, increased SULF1 expression has been linked to endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, cellular senescence, and plaque instability. Its role in pulmonary vascular remodeling remains less certain. The review also considers current inhibitors and other possible approaches to SULF1 modulation. Although SULF1 is accessible in the extracellular space, its therapeutic value is limited by incomplete structural information, weak isoform selectivity, and possible effects on normal vascular repair. Further studies are needed before SULF1 can be regarded as a practical cardiovascular drug target.

articles.title: HER2 as a therapeutic target for CAR T-cell therapy: biological basis, clinical progress, challenges, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR T-cell) therapy is an encouraging immunotherapeutic approach that involves the genetic modification of T lymphocytes to recognize and eliminate cancer cells in a major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-independent manner. Although CAR T-cell therapy has gained significant success in many cancers, its application remains challenging. Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a promising therapeutic target because of its overexpression in many cancers such as gastric, breast, lung, pancreatic, colorectal, ovarian, and other cancers. The central hypothesis of this review is that HER2 represents a uniquely valuable target for solid tumor CAR T-cell engineering because its dense clonal overexpression is essential to maintain tumor suitability and drive cancer stem cell renewal, providing a specific target that can be exploited to bypass resistance mechanisms. Maximizing its clinical potential requires shifting from descriptive platforms to a unified bioengineering paradigm that solves key translational barriers like antigen density discrimination, stromal delivery blockades, heterogeneity-driven escape, and microenvironmental suppression using optimized receptor design. This review provides an overview of CAR T-cell technology and discusses the structure, signaling pathways, and oncogenic role of HER2 in cancer progression. Here, we highlight the preclinical and clinical development of HER2-directed CAR T-cell therapy across different malignancies and highlight the outcomes of ongoing clinical trials. In addition, we discuss the major challenges limiting therapeutic efficacy, including on-target off- tumor toxicity, antigen heterogeneity, limited tumor infiltration, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments, and T-cell exhaustion. Moreover, we cover the emerging strategies designed to overcome these barriers, such as advanced CAR T-cell designs, armored CAR T-cells, dual-targeting approaches, and combination therapies with immune checkpoint inhibitors and radiotherapy. Overall, all of these developments can potentially improve the effectiveness and safety of HER2-targeted CAR T-cell therapy and ensure its future use in oncological treatment.

articles.title: Beyond off-target editing: the emerging landscape of Cas9 cytotoxicity and immunogenicity across biological systems.
articles.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 has transformed agricultural biotechnology, microbial engineering, and human therapeutics within a decade, yet biosafety assessment remains focused on editing accuracy and off-target cleavage. A second, neglected question is what the high-molecular-weight Cas9 effector protein does to expressing systems. This review integrates evidence from eukaryotic cell lines, microbial hosts, transgenic mammals, and dietary exposure models. In isolated cells Cas9 injures the host by three routes, only one requiring DNA cleavage: TP53-dependent genotoxic stress at susceptible loci, modified by cell sex and p53 status; guide-independent binding to ribosomal proteins that activates the PI3K-mTORC2 axis; and promiscuous association with host transcripts inducing a p53-linked stress programme. In GC-rich bacteria, PAM density and limited double-strand break repair make basal expression lethal. Intact mammals tolerate tissue-restricted Cas9 expression, although nervous system and germline compartments are exceptions, and dietary exposure carries no measurable toxicological or allergenic risk. Pre-existing anti-Cas9 immunity is the dominant translational barrier. Proteasomal, SUMO-regulated and autophagic pathways together set Cas9 half-life. Transient ribonucleoprotein delivery, anti-CRISPR, degron-based control, and lower-toxicity orthogonal nucleases each narrow this exposure window. We conclude that Cas9 toxicity is not intrinsic but contingent on expression kinetics, delivery format, host repair, proteostatic capacity, and immunological history. Biosafety is therefore a tunable design parameter, and this review provides a mechanism-based framework for matching nuclease, delivery route and temporal control to the intended application.

articles.title: Adolescent social isolation and re-socialization increases alcohol intake and aversion-resistant drinking in male and female rats.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Adverse experiences during adolescence, especially social isolation, increases risk for alcohol use disorders (AUDs). Previous rodent studies of adolescent social isolation (ASI) encompassed all stages of adolescence and/or maintained isolation into adulthood, limiting identification of vulnerable stages of adolescence. Utilizing males only, or combining the sexes, also may have contributed to contradictory findings. OBJECTIVES: Investigate social isolation restricted to discrete adolescent stages in combination with re-socialization and then persistent alcohol drinking. Determine whether adolescent isolation during specific developmental time periods, with or without subsequent re-socialization, leads to increased alcohol drinking in males or females. METHODS: Male and female Wistar rats underwent one of six housing conditions: (1) isolation from postnatal day (P)21-42 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Early), (2) isolation from P42-63 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Late), or (3) continuous isolation from P21 onward (ASI), or (4​-6) one of three appropriate control treatments. Alcohol-related behaviors were assessed in adulthood using intermittent-access two-bottle choice drinking (IAP), limited daily access (LDA-20) procedures, quinine-adulterated aversion-resistant drinking (ARD), and alcohol re-exposure following prolonged abstinence. RESULTS: In general, ASIR-Early and ASI elevated alcohol drinking in males and females, when compared to contemporary controls, during IAP, LDA-20, ARD, and after prolonged withdrawal, while ASIR-Late had largely similar effects as control conditions. However, for females, only ASI led to greater ARD at the highest quinine dose and also increased alcohol drinking after prolonged withdrawal. In contrast, for males, ASIR-Early and ASI had largely similar enhancement of alcohol drinking. CONCLUSIONS: Under these conditions, isolation housing that encompassed the early adolescent period produced enduring increases in alcohol-related behaviors, with re-socialization perhaps more protective in females against ARD and elevated intake after abstinence. These results inform future studies that will investigate neural mechanisms underlying ASI-induced enhancement of alcohol drinking.

articles.title: Biochanin A attenuates dexamethasone-induced skeletal muscle atrophy with increased SERCA2 expression and reduced mitochondrial injury.
articles.abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced skeletal muscle atrophy involves disrupted proteostasis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and Ca2⁺ homeostasis. SERCA2 may connect Ca2⁺ handling with atrophy signaling. This study aimed to identify and evaluate a candidate intervention for dexamethasone (DEX)-induced skeletal muscle atrophy using SERCA2 expression as a mechanistic lead. Public transcriptomic analysis, in silico gene perturbation, and computational drug screening were integrated to identify potential anti-muscle atrophy compounds. The protective effects of Biochanin A (BCA) were subsequently evaluated in dexamethasone (DEX)-induced C2C12 myotube and mouse muscle atrophy models. ATP2A2 overexpression and siRNA knockdown, combined with molecular, morphological, and mitochondrial functional assays, were performed to investigate the anti-atrophic mechanism of BCA and its association with SERCA2. Computational screening identified Biochanin A (BCA) as a candidate anti-atrophy agent. In vitro, BCA attenuated DEX-induced atrophy marker expression and alleviated mitochondrial damage in C2C12 myotubes without significantly affecting apoptosis. ATP2A2 overexpression increased SERCA2 levels and reduced DEX-associated atrophy-related proteins, whereas BCA-associated reductions in selected proteins were less apparent in the independently normalized siATP2A2 series. In vivo, BCA attenuated DEX-induced losses in muscle mass and function while expanding myofiber size. Consistent with cellular results, BCA upregulated SERCA2 and downregulated p-SMAD3 and S100A4 protein levels in skeletal muscle tissues, whereas total SMAD3 protein expression did not differ significantly. BCA attenuated DEX-induced skeletal muscle atrophy in the experimental models. ATP2A2 overexpression and knockdown altered several atrophy-related protein responses, and BCA coadministration was accompanied by higher SERCA2 expression and reduced mitochondrial injury.

articles.title: Lenabasum attenuates CLP-induced sepsis-associated acute lung injury with coordinated modulation of redox balance and inflammation-resolution profile.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury is a major experimental counterpart of human acute respiratory distress syndrome and involves inflammatory activation, redox imbalance, and structural lung damage. Lenabasum (JBT-101), a selective cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2) agonist, has shown anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties in non-septic inflammation, but its effects in acute polymicrobial sepsis-associated lung injury remain poorly defined. This study evaluated lenabasum in a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced polymicrobial sepsis model during the acute 24-h phase, focusing on lung oxidative/antioxidant indices, the serum inflammation-resolution profile, and histopathological changes. 30 male Wistar rats were allocated to Sham, CLP, CLP + lenabasum 1 mg/kg, CLP + lenabasum 5 mg/kg, or CLP + dexamethasone 1 mg/kg groups. Interventions were administered intraperitoneally after sepsis induction. At 24 h, lung reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), and reduced glutathione (GSH) were measured. Serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-8 (IL-8), C-reactive protein (CRP), and lipoxin A4 (LXA4) were assessed as the inflammation-resolution profile. Lung injury was evaluated under blinded conditions using hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining and lung injury score (LIS). CLP increased lung ROS and MDA, decreased GSH, elevated serum TNF-α, IL-8, CRP, and LXA4, and induced histopathological lung injury. Both lenabasum doses reduced MDA, serum inflammatory markers, and LIS and shifted LXA4 toward Sham levels. At 5 mg/kg, lenabasum also reduced ROS, increased GSH, and attenuated histopathological lung injury. Lenabasum, particularly at 5 mg/kg, attenuated biochemical disturbances and histopathological lung injury at 24 h after CLP. These findings support further preclinical investigation of lenabasum, while the receptor dependence of its effects remains to be established.

articles.title: Integration of machine learning and transcriptomics analysis identifies candidate molecular associations between parthenolide and sepsis-associated acute lung injury.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are both life-threatening diseases. Sepsis-related ALI frequently presents with complications of sepsis, which are mostly identified by the presence of non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and refractory hypoxia. Despite the advancements in the field of drug discovery and delivery science, the understanding and management of sepsis-associated ALI are insufficient. WGCNA and differential expression analyses were integrated across multiple transcriptomics database cohorts to determine the core common candidate genes associated with sepsis-associated ALI and PTL. A Lasso model with SHAP interpretability was trained for feature selection. Molecular docking was performed for all candidate targets using PyRx with AutoDock Vina as the docking engine. Intersection of predicted parthenolide (PTL) targets and ALI-associated genes yielded 17 candidate genes. The Lasso algorithm used nested cross-validation, yielding an AUC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.767-0.928) and external validation with AUC values of 0.918 (GSE76293) and 0.667 (GSE10361). Molecular docking analysis indicated that the potential binding energies of the selected targets were - 5.9 to - 8.5 kcal/mol. These computational findings identify candidate PTL-associated molecular targets and provide a structural hypothesis to guide experimental validation.

articles.title: Bioactive laponite-reinforced thermosensitive PVA/Pluronic F127 hydrogel incorporating PRP and β-glucan: formulation, characterization, and preliminary in vivo evaluation.
articles.abstract: Beta-glucans are natural polysaccharides with immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and tissue-regenerative properties, while platelet-rich plasma (PRP) supplies growth factors supporting cell proliferation and angiogenesis. We formulated and characterized a thermosensitive, sprayable hydrogel combining polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), Pluronic F127, Laponite, beta-glucan, and PRP, designed to be semi-liquid at room temperature and to gel near body temperature (37 °C) for in situ application to irregular wounds. A three-factor Box-Behnken design was used to investigate formulation composition and gelation-related properties. A practical formulation containing 3.5% (w/v) PVA, 10% (w/v) Poloxamer 407, 4% (w/v) Laponite, 2% (w/v) β-glucan, and 1% (v/v) PRP was selected for experimental characterization based on gelation temperature, gelation time, and stability. Rheological analysis demonstrated temperature-dependent viscoelastic behavior, while FTIR and SEM provided information on possible intermolecular interactions and the morphology of the freeze dried hydrogel. Mass-loss testing revealed limited persistence under the investigated aqueous conditions. The formulation was evaluated in a full-thickness excisional wound model in Wistar rats over a 14-day observation period. Wound area and diameter did not differ significantly among groups (P = 0.274 and P = 0.582, respectively). Blinded semi-quantitative histology (n = 3 per group per time point) showed normal healing progression in all groups with only small differences among groups (not statistically tested); the complete beta-glucan/PRP formulation showed numerical trends toward higher scores at day 14. These findings support the feasibility of the developed hydrogel as a thermoresponsive topical formulation; however, enhanced wound healing efficacy was not demonstrated, and further formulation refinement and biological evaluation are required.

articles.title: Metabolic, Hepatic, and Neuropathological Effects of Palm11-PrRP31 and Liraglutide in High-Fat Diet-Fed APP/PS1 Mice.
articles.abstract: Metabolic stress is known to accelerate Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression. In our previous study, we demonstrated that long-term high-fat diet (HFD) feeding exacerbated not only amyloid-β (Aβ) burden but also liver steatosis in APP/PS1 mice, a transgenic model of AD, with effects worsening with age. The present study investigated whether a three-month treatment (from 6 to 9 months of age) with anorexigenic peptides (palm11-PrRP31 or liraglutide) could attenuate AD-like pathology, neuroinflammation, liver steatosis, and Aβ clearance in APP/PS1 male mice on HFD. The two compounds exhibited distinct therapeutic effects. Liraglutide reduced body weight and improved glucose tolerance in both genotypes, while also attenuating insulin resistance in APP/PS1 mice. In contrast, palm11-PrRP31 significantly reduced Aβ plaque burden and showed a tendency to decrease astrocytosis. Notably, both peptides markedly reduced microgliosis and pathological tau phosphorylation at Ser202 and Thr205 in the hippocampus and cerebral cortex.
