HFD induced pronounced hepatic steatosis in both genotypes; however, APP/PS1 mice exhibited more severe lipid imbalance, characterized by increased triacylglycerols and decreased phospholipids and cardiolipins compared to wild-type controls. While both compounds reduced liver steatosis and inflammation in wild-type mice, only liraglutide normalized lipid composition in APP/PS1 mice. Furthermore, Aβ deposits colocalized with CD11b clusters were absent in the liver of liraglutide-treated APP/PS1 mice. In conclusion, both peptides exert neuroprotective effects under metabolic stress, but through distinct mechanisms. Palm11-PrRP31 primarily reduces amyloid pathology and neuroinflammation, whereas liraglutide acts mainly through metabolic improvement.

articles.title: Distinct patterns of activity in the prelimbic cortex track task-related differences for cocaine and water reinforcers.
articles.abstract: The pursuit of drugs is a fundamental element of substance use. Different tasks assess drug pursuit in the face of effort, punishment, or the absence of the drug, and recent studies have suggested that a shared latent variable may drive behavior across these tasks. The prelimbic cortex (PL) is implicated in these behaviors, but it is unknown if its role is driven by distinct neural ensembles. We recorded PL activity using in vivo endoscopic calcium imaging in 32 male and female Sprague-Dawley rats as they completed cocaine or water self-administration, extinction, progressive ratio, and punished self-administration. We found that behavior across tasks covaried in water, but not cocaine rats. We also found that slow, sustained neural excitations following response for reward were lower in extinction. Furthermore, exploratory analysis suggests that those individual rats that had more responsive neurons also had significantly higher levels of reward pursuit in the extinction task. Notably, this relationship was true across cocaine and water rats, suggesting a general role independent of reward type. Thus, our findings suggest that extinction behavior is tracked by a distinct neural pattern in the PL.

articles.title: In vitro anthelmintic activity and safety profile of leaf and root extracts of Vernonia amygdalina against adult Onchocerca ochengi.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Vernonia amygdalina is widely used in Cameroon folk medicine for intestinal worms, schistosomiasis and filarial-related conditions. Ethnobotanical surveys in Adamawa, including Ngaoundere, report its antifilarial use with high frequency indices among traditional healers. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the in vitro anthelmintic activity and safety profile of leaf and root extracts of V. amygdalina against adult male Onchocerca ochengi. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Aqueous and ethanolic extracts were prepared by maceration. In vitro anthelmintic activity was tested against Onchocerca ochengi males at different concentrations (1 worm/well and 6 worm/concentration). Acute toxicity was evaluated in mice at 2000 mg/kg (OECD 423, 14 days). For sub-acute toxicity, 40 mice (5 males and 5 females/group, n ⹀ 10) received 0, 250, 500 and 1000 mg/kg b.w. of root aqueous extract orally (OECD 407). Organ weights, hematology, AST/ALT, lipid profile, creatinine and total protein were evaluated (ANOVA + Dunnett). RESULTS: Phytochemical screening revealed saponins, flavonoids, tannins, and alkaloids. All extracts showed concentration-and time-dependent activity. Aqueous root extract was the most potent with LC50 40.24 ± 1.15 μg/mL at 48 h and 100% mortality at 100 μg/mL (ivermectin LC50 of 17.78 ± 2.01 μg/mL). LD50 >2000 mg/kg. All hematological parameters showed significant variations (p ⹀ 0.019 to < 0.0001) except MCV (p ⹀ 0.064) and MPV (p ⹀ 0.34). Liver (p ⹀ 0.321) and heart weights (p ⹀ 0.052) were unchanged. Despite increased kidney (p ⹀ 0.009) and spleen (p < 0.0001) weights (marked splenomegaly), histology remained normal. Total cholesterol (p < 0.0001), triglycerides (p < 0.0001), HDL (p ⹀ 0.017), LDL (p ⹀ 0.0002) and total protein (p < 0.0001) were decreased in all treated groups, indicating hypolipidemic activity. Creatinine remained unchanged (p ⹀ 0.627). No AST/ALT co-elevation. CONCLUSIONS: Root aqueous extract showed potent anthelmintic activity supporting traditional use with hypolipidemic effect. No hepato, cardio or nephrotoxicity was observed. The NOAEL was considered to be 500 mg/kg b.w., with mild and reversible high-dose splenomegaly and hypoproteinemia without histological lesions at 1000 mg/kg, indicating a wide safety margin.

articles.title: Chang-Yan-Ning Granules Attenuates Colitis-Associated Intestinal Barrier Damage by Acting on SSTR1 to Suppress Inflammatory Responses.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Chang-Yan-Ning Granules (CYN) is a traditional Chinese herbal formula widely used in the clinical management of ulcerative colitis (UC). However, its molecular mechanisms of action, particularly with respect to intestinal barrier protection, remain incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to systematically investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of CYN in colitis, with a focus on identifying its functional molecular targets and bioactive constituents. METHODS: A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced acute colitis mouse model was established to evaluate the in vivo efficacy of CYN. Integrated approaches combining RNA sequencing, network pharmacology prediction, chemical profiling, and public database mining were employed to predict candidate targets. Multi-scale in vitro and vivo validation was performed using THP-1 co-cultured intestinal epithelial cells, mouse colonic organoids, and a zebrafish model of UC. Somatostatin receptor 1 (SSTR1) functional validation was conducted via siRNA-mediated knockdown. RESULTS: CYN treatment reduced disease activity index (DAI) scores, partially restored colonic length, preserved colonic crypt architecture, and increased occludin expression in DSS-treated mice. Across the cell co-culture and colonic organoid models, CYN suppressed inflammatory responses and preserved epithelial barrier integrity, as indicated by reduced TNF-α and IL-6 levels and improved expression or junctional distribution of occludin and ZO-1. In zebrafish, CYN reduced intestinal neutrophil accumulation and ameliorated model-associated alterations in goblet cells and intestinal morphology. Transcriptomic and network pharmacology analyses revealed enrichment of inflammation-related pathways and identified SSTR1 as a candidate mediator associated with the protective effects of CYN. Rutin and rosmarinic acid (RA), two blood-absorbed constituents of CYN, exhibited barrier-protective and anti-inflammatory activities. Drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) and molecular docking analyses provided complementary evidence supporting potential interactions between rutin or RA and SSTR1. The protective effects of CYN and both constituents were markedly attenuated following SSTR1 knockdown. Further pathway analysis revealed reduced MEK phosphorylation following treatment with CYN and its candidate active constituents, whereas no significant changes were detected in ERK, AKT, or STAT3 under the conditions examined. CONCLUSION: CYN alleviates experimental colitis and preserves intestinal barrier integrity. Rutin and RA were identified as blood-absorbed constituents of CYN, may contribute to its barrier-protective and anti-inflammatory effects. Functional knockdown experiments, together with DARTS and molecular docking analyses, support SSTR1 as a potential mediator associated with the protective effects of CYN and its bioactive constituents, although direct target engagement and the precise causal relationship remain to be established. The observed reduction in MEK phosphorylation suggests a possible association between MEK-related signaling and the protective effects of CYN. These findings provide a basis for further elucidating the pharmacological effects of CYN in UC and highlight the potential relevance of SSTR1-associated signaling to intestinal barrier protection.

articles.title: Xiongma decoction alleviates cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion injury in association with gut microbiota remodelling and attenuation of TLR4/NF-κB signalling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Xiongma decoction (XMD), a traditional herbal formula comprising Ligusticum chuanxiong Hort. and Gastrodia elata Bl., has long been used to treat headache and dizziness. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the neuroprotective effects of XMD against cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) and examine the contribution of gut microbiota and associated inflammatory changes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Rats received XMD for 14 days after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R). Neurological function, infarct volume, brain oedema, neuronal injury, inflammatory responses, barrier-associated markers and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) levels were assessed. Faecal microbiota and fatty acids were profiled by shotgun metagenomic sequencing and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, respectively. Antibiotic depletion and faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) before MCAO/R were used to examine the contribution of gut microbiota. RESULTS: XMD improved neurological function and reduced cerebral infarction, oedema, neuronal injury and inflammation. It remodelled faecal microbiota, increased faecal butyrate, preserved colonic tight-junction protein expression and epithelial ultrastructure, and lowered serum and brain LPS levels. Brain immunoglobulin G and serum S100B levels were reduced. XMD also attenuated microglial activation and cerebral TLR4/MYD88/NF-κB signalling. Pro-inflammatory cytokines were negatively correlated with tight-junction protein expression in brain and colonic tissues. Antibiotic pretreatment attenuated XMD-associated neuroprotection, while FMT from XMD-treated donors partially reproduced the neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects in recipient rats. CONCLUSION: XMD alleviated CIRI in rats, with evidence supporting a contribution of gut microbiota to protection. Higher faecal butyrate and attenuated cerebral inflammatory signalling accompanied these effects.

articles.title: Gancao Xiexin Decoction Ameliorates Experimental Colitis and Reduces Colonic CD4+ Tissue-Resident Memory T-Cell Accumulation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Gancao Xiexin Decoction (GXD) is a traditional Chinese herbal formula historically used for gastrointestinal disorders characterized by mixed cold-heat patterns and has subsequently been applied in the treatment of UC (ulcerative colitis). Although its protective effects against experimental colitis have been reported, whether these effects are associated with regulation of pathogenic mucosal immune-memory populations remains unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigated whether the anti-colitic effects of GXD are associated with regulation of colonic CD4+ tissue-resident memory T (CD4+ TRM) cells and examined the potential contribution of microbiota-dependent bile acid remodeling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical profile of GXD was characterized by LC-MS, and its effects were evaluated in mice with dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis. Colonic CD4+ TRM cells were quantified using multicolor flow cytometry and multiplex immunofluorescence. Metagenomic sequencing, fecal metabolomics, antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation, ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) supplementation, and pharmacological VDR inhibition were used to investigate the involvement of microbiota-dependent bile acid remodeling and VDR signaling. RESULTS: GXD ameliorated colonic injury and reduced colonic CD4+ TRM-cell accumulation in mice with DSS-induced colitis. GXD also altered the gut microbiota and fecal metabolite profiles and increased fecal UDCA levels. Antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion attenuated, whereas transplantation of microbiota from GXD-treated donors partially transferred, the effects of GXD on colitis and CD4+ TRM-cell accumulation. Exogenous UDCA alleviated colitis and reduced colonic CD4+ TRM accumulation in mice with and without antibiotic pretreatment. UDCA increased VDR expression in a sorted colonic CD4+ CD103+ T-cell population, and pharmacological VDR inhibition partially attenuated the effects of UDCA. CONCLUSIONS: GXD ameliorated experimental colitis and reduced colonic CD4+ TRM-cell accumulation in association with microbiota-dependent bile acid remodeling. The findings further support the involvement of UDCA and VDR signaling in this immunomodulatory effect. To our knowledge, this is the first study to link the anti-colitic effects of GXD to the regulation of colonic CD4+ TRM cells.

articles.title: Jaeumganghwa-tang, a Korean National Health Insurance herbal extract, ameliorates polycystic ovary syndrome related ovarian dysfunction with reduced apoptotic stress and improved FSH-responsive steroidogenesis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) still remains understudied in the face of 8-13% prevalence in reproductive women. This study investigated the effects of Jaeumganghwa-tang (JGT), a Korean National Health Insurance herbal extract, on PCOS-related ovarian dysfunction and associated changes in apoptosis and FSH-responsive steroidogenesis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Network pharmacology identified overlapping targets between JGT and PCOS, followed by comprehensive functional enrichment analysis. Letrozole-induced PCOS rats received oral JGT (0.3, 0.6, 1.2 g/kg) for 4 weeks. Ovarian morphology, estrous cyclicity, apoptosis, ovarian hormone-responsive and steroidogenic markers, and circulating LH, FSH, and testosterone were assessed. CdCl2-exposed KGN cells were used for analyzing mitochondrial integrity with JC-10 and ATP, and FSH-induced cAMP signaling. RESULTS: Network analysis identified 16 overlapping genes, including BCL2, BAX, and CYP19A1, with enrichment in apoptosis- and ovarian steroidogenesis-related pathways. JGT attenuated estrous-cycle disruption, cystic follicular accumulation, and endometrial thinning. Letrozole increased serum LH and testosterone; JGT reduced LH at 0.6 and 1.2 g/kg and testosterone at 1.2 g/kg, whereas FSH was not altered by letrozole. JGT also modulated ovarian AMH/AMHR2 and hormone-receptor expression and partially recovered steroidogenic markers. In KGN cells, JGT improved mitochondrial function, reduced apoptotic stress, enhanced FSH-induced cAMP signaling, and restored StAR, CYP19A1, and HSD3B expression together with estradiol and progesterone production. CONCLUSION: JGT attenuated PCOS-related ovarian abnormalities and selected endocrine disturbances during letrozole exposure, accompanied by reduced apoptotic stress and improved FSH-responsive steroidogenic function. These associations warrant further causal validation.

articles.title: Integrating Mouse Transcriptomics and Human Multi-Cohort Data Reveals an Inflammatory Gene Signature Mediating Jaceosidin's Therapeutic Effect in Ulcerative Colitis.
articles.abstract: Jaceosidin exerts protective effects against ulcerative colitis (UC), but its molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study integrates transcriptomics, machine learning, and co-expression network analysis to elucidate Jaceosidin's targets in UC. A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse colitis model with transcriptome sequencing was established. Core genes were identified by WGCNA and cross-dataset analysis of public UC datasets. Three machine learning algorithms constructed a risk prediction model. GO/KEGG, GSEA, immune infiltration, and single-cell analyses were performed. In vivo validation included enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10) and Western blot for core proteins and NF-κB. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) explored causality. Forty-one core genes were narrowed to four (CXCL3, LCN2, LMCD1, S100A9) by machine learning. The model achieved AUC > 0.9. GSEA linked the four genes to NF-κB signaling and immune infiltration. ELISA confirmed Jaceosidin reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6 and elevated IL-10. Western blot confirmed NF-κB suppression. MR for LCN2 showed no causal effect on UC risk (p = 0.682), supporting these genes as downstream effectors. Jaceosidin alleviated colitis and downregulated the four genes. Jaceosidin ameliorates UC by modulating a four-gene module and inhibiting NF-κB-mediated inflammation. The model provides new targets for UC treatment monitoring.

articles.title: OSBPL3 promotes pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progression through lipid metabolism reprogramming and is targeted by lupenone.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: As a highly malignant neoplasm with dismal prognosis, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is closely linked to disordered lipid metabolism, which serves a key part in facilitating its pathological progression. Identifying key lipid metabolism-related genes as therapeutic targets is urgent. METHODS: Differentially expressed genes in PDAC were screened using GEO datasets and overlapped with lipid metabolism-related genes via Venn diagram. OSBPL3 was identified as a crucial regulator in the PDAC development through expression and survival analysis. In vitro (CCK-8, Transwell, BODIPY staining, Fillipin III staining) and in vivo (xenograft models) experiments assessed its functions on PDAC progression and lipid metabolism. Molecular docking identified Lupenone as an OSBPL3 inhibitor, with validation of its effects on cell proliferation and lipid metabolism. RESULTS: OSBPL3 was remarkably upregulated in PDAC tissues and cell lines (PANC-1, BxPC-3), correlating with poor survival. Knockdown of OSBPL3 attenuated cell viability, migration, and tumor growth, accelerated apoptosis, and suppressed lipid accumulation (lipid droplets, cholesterol, triglycerides), reduced the expression of SREBP1, ACLY, and ACC1. Lupenone targeted OSBPL3, reversed its pro-tumor effects, and reduced lipid metabolism. CONCLUSION: OSBPL3 drives PDAC progression via lipid metabolism regulation, and Lupenone is a potential therapeutic agent targeting OSBPL3.

articles.title: Vitamin D3 Attenuates Experimental Colitis with PPARγ-associated regulation of macrophage lipid accumulation.
articles.abstract: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) and its active metabolite calcitriol exert immunoregulatory effects, but their macrophage metabolic actions during intestinal inflammation remain incompletely defined. We examined oral vitamin D3 in experimental colitis and explored vitamin D receptor (VDR)-associated peroxisome proliferator-activated receptorγ (PPARγ) involvement in macrophage responses to calcitriol. In a dextran sulfate sodium-induced mouse model, oral vitamin D3 reduced disease activity, colonic injury, macrophage infiltration and inflammatory cytokine production, and partly normalized selected serum lipid parameters, with dose-related increases in serum 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (1,25-(OH)2D3). In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated bone marrow-derived macrophages, calcitriol lowered IL-6 and IL-12/23p40, increased IL-10 and TGF-β, reduced M1-like/M2-like macrophage ratio, and decreased intracellular triglyceride, cholesterol and lipid-droplet accumulation. Oral vitamin D3 restored colonic PPARγ expression, PPARγ knockdown attenuated the effects of calcitriol on cytokine release and lipid accumulation. Murine colon microarray data linked myeloid Pparg deficiency to higher expression of inflammatory genes and lower expression of selected lipid-metabolism genes. Human UC macrophages with detectable VDR transcripts had higher PPARγ-target and lipid-metabolism module scores. These findings support anti-colitic effects of oral vitamin D3 and suggest VDR-associated PPARγ involvement in the macrophage response to calcitriol.

articles.title: Tubular EZH2-HIF1α axis promotes mouse renal fibrosis after ischemia-reperfusion-induced acute kidney injury by accelerating cellular senescence.
articles.abstract: Maladaptive tubular repair and cellular senescence contribute to the transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD), but the associated regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the involvement of EZH2- and HIF-1α-associated signaling in tubular senescence and renal fibrosis. A murine unilateral ischemia-reperfusion injury model combined with contralateral nephrectomy was used to examine AKI-to-CKD progression, and DZNep was administered to evaluate its pharmacological effects. Hypoxia/reoxygenation- and TGF-β1-stimulated tubular epithelial cells were used for complementary in vitro analyses. EZH2 and HIF-1α remained elevated during post-ischemic kidney injury, whereas DZNep treatment improved renal function and attenuated tubular damage, fibrosis, and senescence-associated changes. In HK-2 cells, DZNep and 2-MeOE2 reduced injury-, fibrosis-, and senescence-related responses. To strengthen target-specific evidence, EZH2 knockdown attenuated H/R-induced HIF-1α expression, SASP production, and α-SMA and FN accumulation. Similarly, HIF1A knockdown reduced EZH2 expression and the induction of SASP and profibrotic proteins following H/R. These genetic findings support the involvement of both EZH2 and HIF-1α in the cellular response to ischemic stress, although they do not establish direct regulation or a feedback loop. Collectively, EZH2- and HIF-1α-associated signaling may contribute to maladaptive tubular senescence and fibrotic remodeling after AKI and warrants further mechanistic evaluation.

articles.title: Mucoadhesive dual-extrusion 3D-printed bilayer buccal films for enhanced paediatric delivery of azithromycin.
articles.abstract: Paediatric administration of azithromycin (AZT) is often limited by low bioavailability (∼37%) and poor patient compliance associated with conventional oral dosage forms. In this study, novel mucoadhesive bilayer buccal films were developed using a dual-extrusion 3D printing strategy to enhance transmucosal delivery and ensure unidirectional drug diffusion. The hydrophilic mucoadhesive layer was formulated using sodium hyaluronate and Soluplus®, incorporating either crystalline AZT, crystalline AZT with formulation enhancers (bile salts or sucrose palmitate), or a co-amorphous system, i.e., AZT-caprylic acid (AZT-ACPL). Rheological investigations showed optimal thixotropic recovery of the hydrogel inks for semi-solid extrusion. In addition, the bilayer films were fabricated in a single-step, continuous process using a combined dual-extrusion 3D printing system, where a flexible hydrophobic polycaprolactone backing layer was deposited via melt-based extrusion to prevent salivary wash-out and promote unidirectional drug diffusion. Solid-state analyses (XRPD, FTIR, SEM) showed structural component integrity and predominantly amorphous, highly homogeneous drug dispersion of AZT-ACPL in the loaded matrix. Incorporating the co-amorphous AZT-ACPL significantly boosted maximum water uptake compared to its crystalline counterpart. Ex-vivo permeation studies across porcine oesophageal mucosa demonstrated superior mucosal transport for the co-amorphous formulation, achieving ∼ 18% cumulative permeation after 6 h: more than 3-fold enhancement in permeation compared to crystalline AZT formulations and powder drug control. Ex-vivo mechanical testing demonstrated effective mucosal adhesion while the protective backing layer sustained mucosal residence for over 4 h by shielding the hydrogel from erosion. Overall, this dual-extrusion 3D printing technology holds the potential to offer a robust, and customizable strategy for personalized transmucosal drug delivery.

articles.title: RVG29-modified reduction-responsive nanomicelles for brain-targeted delivery of a glutaminyl cyclase inhibitor in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Although glutaminyl cyclase (QC)-mediated formation of pyroglutamate-modified amyloid-β (pE-Aβ) has been implicated as an upstream pathological event in Alzheimer's disease (AD), the therapeutic translation of small-molecule QC inhibitors remains limited by insufficient brain exposure. Here, we developed a reduction-responsive polymeric micellar platform (designated PIC) based on poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-poly(aspartic acid) (PAsp)-poly(valine) (PVal) copolymers. This platform was functionalized with rabies virus glycoprotein-derived peptide 29 (RVG29) to obtain RVG29-PIC-B13 for enhanced brain delivery of B13, an imidazole-based QC inhibitor, and release of its active thiol form. B13 was conjugated to PEG-PAsp-PVal micelles through a disulfide linker, whereas RVG29 was introduced as a brain-targeting ligand to enhance blood-brain barrier transport. RVG29-PIC-B13 formed spherical nanomicelles with an average diameter of 169.9 nm, a drug-loading content of 6.2%, high colloidal stability, and glutathione-triggered release of B13-SH, which retained QC inhibitory activity with an IC50 of 1.17 μM. RVG29 modification significantly enhanced cellular uptake in bEND.3, PC12, and SH-SY5Y cells, increased transport across a bEND.3 monolayer by 3.12-fold, and elevated brain fluorescence accumulation in vivo by 2.58-fold and 1.96-fold compared with free Cy5 and unmodified micelles, respectively. In 8-month-old 3 × Tg-AD mice, 45-day administration of RVG29-PIC-B13 significantly improved performance in the Morris water maze, Y-maze, open-field, and elevated plus maze assays. Mechanistically, RVG29-PIC-B13 inhibited brain QC activity without markedly altering QC expression, reduced Aβ and pE-Aβ burden, attenuated AT8/AT100-associated tau phosphorylation, and preserved dendritic complexity and spine density. Preliminary hematological and histological analyses indicated acceptable biocompatibility. These findings support RVG29-PIC-B13 as a promising reduction-responsive nanodelivery strategy for enhancing brain delivery of QC inhibitors and improving therapeutic outcomes in AD.

articles.title: Transdermal delivery of cobimetinib via HPMC gel combining menthol and iontophoresis for locoregional melanoma treatment.
articles.abstract: Orally administered cobimetinib (COBI), a selective MEK1/2 inhibitor is effective against melanoma but is associated with systemic adverse events. Herein, the HPMC-based gel combining menthol and iontophoresis was developed for locoregional transdermal delivery of COBI. Formulation was optimized via single-factor screening and an L9(33) orthogonal design. Optimized gels exhibited acceptable rheological properties and physical stability under stress conditions. In vitro permeation using excised rat abdominal skin revealed that 5% (w/w) menthol significantly enhanced COBI permeation, while iontophoresis was optimized at 3 h with 0.45% (w/w) NaCl. Based on the in vitro optimization, 0.8% (w/w) COBI loading was selected as the medium-dose candidate for subsequent in vivo efficacy evaluation (with 0.4% and 1.2% evaluated as low and high doses, respectively). In B16F10 cells, COBI combined with mild direct current showed greater inhibition of cell viability than either treatment alone. In tumor-bearing C57BL/6 mice, the optimized gelplus iontophoresis achieved achieved a tumor-weight inhibition rate of 98.2%, with histological findings suggesting increased tumor necrosis and reduced proliferation. At an equivalent dose, passive transdermal administration produced lower systemic exposure than oral dosing, whereas iontophoresis achieved comparable systemic exposure to passive delivery at half the nominal dose. In a separate mouse study, selected transdermal regimens exhibited higher tumor-to-plasma concentration ratios than oral administration at a single sampling time point. Collectively, this study demonstrates that the HPMC gel combining menthol and iontophoresis enables effective local tumor suppression.

articles.title: An oil-protected microemulsion strategy overcomes ionic liquids instability in the gastrointestinal tract for enhanced oral drug delivery.
articles.abstract: The oral delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs and peptide therapeutics is often hindered by their low solubility, poor permeability, and susceptibility to enzymatic degradation within the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. While ionic liquids (ILs) can improve drug solubility and stability, the performance of IL-containing formulations can be compromised by rapid dilution and ion-pair dissociation in the aqueous GI environment. To address this instability, we developed a self-emulsifying IL-based microemulsion platform (IL-ME). This system was constructed using choline geranate ([Ch][GA]) IL, medium-chain triglycerides as the oil phase, and optimized surfactants. To evaluate the versatility of the platform across different drug classes, paclitaxel (PTX, a poorly soluble small molecule) and semaglutide (Sema, a peptide) were selected as two model drugs. The formulation was designed to retard aqueous dilution and preserve IL functionality during GI transit. After incubation in simulated GI fluids, >70% of the loaded paclitaxel remained dissolved in the IL-ME formulations, whereas <50% remained dissolved in the plain IL, indicating substantially enhanced GI stability of the IL-MEs. In vitro enzymatic degradation studies revealed that the IL-MEs resisted trypsin digestion and maintained semaglutide stability against pepsin degradation over 90 min. Pharmacokinetic studies showed that IL-MEs enhanced oral bioavailability of paclitaxel by 4.02-fold and semaglutide by 2.89-fold relative to plain IL formulations. In vivo fluorescence tracking using an aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) probe demonstrated prolonged GI retention, with >65% of fluorescence signal preserved 10 h after administration. Safety evaluation showed no significant toxicity or intestinal inflammation after repeated oral dosing. This work presents a formulation strategy that enhances IL stability in the GI tract through oil-mediated retardation of aqueous dilution, offering a promising approach for enhancing the oral delivery of both small-molecule and peptide drugs.

articles.title: Poricoic acid A enhances paclitaxel sensitivity in emotional distress-associated breast cancer via NPY1R/ERK signaling.
articles.abstract: Emotional distress (ED) represents a prevalent psychological comorbidity in patients with breast cancer (BC), serving as a critical driver of accelerated tumor progression and compromised chemotherapy outcomes. Poricoic acid A (PAA), a bioactive triterpenoid isolated from Poria cocos, is recognized for its sedative and putative antitumor properties; however, its therapeutic potential and the molecular underpinnings governing its influence on ED-associated BC (ED-BC) remain poorly explored. Here, we demonstrate that ED exacerbates BC growth in mouse models and significantly impairs the antitumor efficacy of paclitaxel (PTX), as evidenced by a decline in the tumor volume inhibition rate from 38.69% to 26.59%. Administration of PAA not only significantly mitigated depressive-like behaviors but also reinstated PTX sensitivity. Notably, the combination of high-dose PAA and PTX achieved a tumor inhibition rate of 65.93% without obvious systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, PAA was found to suppress neuropeptide Y (NPY) -induced activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) signaling cascade by targeting the neuropeptide Y receptor 1 (NPY1R), thereby attenuating ED-BC progression and augmenting the pro-apoptotic effects of PTX. Collectively, these findings identify the NPY1R/ERK-mediated neuro-tumor axis as a mechanistic link between emotional distress and reduced PTX responsiveness. Our findings support the further development of PAA as a potential natural adjunct to chemotherapy and provide a rationale for future clinical evaluation of stress-related phenotyping and molecular stratification in patients with BC.

articles.title: Centrifugal filters for time-efficient and waste-reducing lab-scale purification of lipid nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNP) are amongst the most clinically tested non-viral systems for the delivery of nucleic acids. Therefore, different production parameters have been thoroughly investigated and optimized in efforts to increase LNP quality and stability. A critical step in LNP manufacturing is purification, in which the exchange of production buffer against buffer systems with physiological pH removes residual ethanol and neutralizes the ionizable lipid. Purification is commonly performed via dialysis, a process that has the downside of being time-consuming and generating high waste volumes. In this work, we propose a purification protocol of 3hours using centrifugal filters, which reduces buffer waste and allows a single-day LNP production in a more workload-friendly manner. For that, different purification devices were investigated for the lab-scale purification of LNP. In the study, nucleic acids ranging from 20 to 1980 nucleotides were used, so that findings cover a broad range of commonly investigated payloads. We also assessed the in-use short time stability of commonly used lipids and give insights into the use of empty LNP for optimization.

articles.title: Influence of supersaturation and precipitation inhibition on the biopharmaceutical performance of olaparib loaded Type IV lipid-based formulations.
articles.abstract: Supersaturation offers a strategy to overcome drug-loading limitations of lipid-based formulations (LBFs), but whether increased drug loading and post-dispersion drug availability translate into enhanced oral exposure remains unclear. This study investigated supersaturated Type IV LBFs (Super-Type IV) and the role of poly (vinylpyrrolidone-co-vinyl acetate) (PVP-VA) in stabilizing the supersaturated state of olaparib. Type IV LBFs comprising Labrasol and Transcutol P were prepared as conventional, thermally supersaturated, and supersaturated formulations containing 5 % w/w PVP-VA. Formulations were evaluated for colloidal properties, aqueous-phase distribution, permeation, and oral pharmacokinetic. Thermal processing increased olaparib loading by approximately 148 % relative to equilibrium solubility. During lipolysis, PVP-VA effectively reduced drug precipitation, below 5 % and maintained highest supersaturation ratio. The Super-Type IV PVP-VA formulation exhibited the highest numerical permeability flux, although differences among Type IV LBFs were non-significant. A Gelucire 44/14-based suspension showed comparatively lower in vitro drug distribution and permeation. In vivo, both Super-Type IV LBFs significantly increased Cmax versus conventional LBF, whereas only Super-Type IV PVP-VA significantly increased AUC; differences between the two supersaturated formulations were non-significant. Overall, supersaturation increased drug loading and aqueous-phase availability, while PVP-VA enhanced exposure without a proportional increase in permeability, highlighting the complex relationship between formulation-level drug availability and oral absorption.

articles.title: Deprivation of branched-chain amino acids improves hepatic glucose metabolism in the absence of acute insulin stimulation.
articles.abstract: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA), i.e., Leu, Ile, and Val, are associated with insulin resistance, and dietary BCAA restriction has been reported to improve glucose homeostasis. However, the hepatic responses associated with BCAA depletion and their relationship to acute insulin stimulation require further clarification. Here, we evaluated glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and hepatic glucose metabolism in mice and examined the expression of key metabolic genes in HepG2 cells cultured under BCAA depletion, with or without acute insulin stimulation. BCAA depletion improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity alongside lower food intake and body weight. Hepatic expression of several glucogenic regulators, including pyruvate carboxylase (PC), Forkhead box O1 (FOXO1), and phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 2 (PEPCK), was reduced under BCAA depletion with PC showing a similar response with or without exogenous insulin stimulation. PAS staining showed that BCAA depletion increases hepatic glycogen accumulation alongside reduced expression of glycogen synthase kinase 3 alpha (GSK3α), glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK3β), and glycogen phosphorylase L (PYGL), which is suggestive of decreased glycogen breakdown capacity. BCAA depletion increased inhibin subunit βE (INHBE) mRNA expression and without insulin stimulated hepatic mRNA and protein expression of fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21); insulin further enhanced this response. Finally, BCAA deprivation promoted fatty acid oxidation and suppressed lipogenesis and lipid uptake transcripts despite exogenous insulin stimulation. These findings suggest that BCAA depletion was associated with improved whole-body glucose handling and coordinated hepatic metabolic responses with selected responses occurring in the absence of acute insulin stimulation.

articles.title: Juglone exerts acaricidal activity against Sarcoptes scabiei via dual inhibition of mite mitochondrial complexes III and IV for scabies control.
articles.abstract: Scabies is a globally prevalent neglected tropical disease affecting approximately 500 million people. While juglone exhibits promising acaricidal properties, its molecular targets and underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. This study aimed to elucidate juglone's binding interactions, acaricidal mechanisms, and species specificity using surface plasmon resonance (SPR), RNA-Seq analysis, molecular docking, Western blotting, and enzyme activity assays. The results reveal that juglone demonstrates significant acaricidal activity against Sarcoptes scabiei and Psoroptes cuniculi. Mechanistically, it dual-targets cytochrome b (Cyt b) and cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 (COX-1) to inhibit mitochondrial respiratory complexes III and IV. Through hydrogen bonding and π-alkyl interactions, juglone induces electron transport collapse, with 40 μg/mL yielding inhibition rates of 48.94% and 66.51% for complexes III and IV, respectively. This respiratory chain dysfunction triggers excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, impairs energy metabolism, and disrupts mitochondrial homeostasis via excessive fission and mitophagy, ultimately causing irreversible structural damage. Furthermore, juglone exhibited distinct species specificity; it significantly inhibited mitochondrial membrane potential and complex activity in C6/36 cells but showed no activity in RAW264.7 cells, indicating that insect cells are particularly sensitive to juglone (i.e., the C6/36 cell line). In conclusion, juglone exerts robust acaricidal effects by disrupting mitochondrial quality control and energy metabolism via complexes III and IV, laying the foundation for its development as a novel alternative acaricidal agent.

articles.title: Preclinical characterization of DK-AT390HCl, a potent PIKfyve inhibitor in colorectal cancer models.
articles.abstract: PIKfyve regulates endolysosomal trafficking and late-stage autophagic processing, making it a therapeutic target in pathway-dependent tumors. This study characterized the preclinical activity, target-binding profile, pharmacokinetics, and antitumor efficacy of the 1,3,5-triazine derivative DK-AT390HCl in colorectal cancer models. DK-AT390HCl bound PIKfyve with high affinity (Kd = 5.6 nM), inhibited its kinase activity in an ADP-Glo assay (IC₅₀ = 21.5 nM) and showed favorable kinase-panel selectivity. It inhibited proliferation of murine CT26 and human SW480 and SW620 cells, with IC50 values of 8.6-15.9 µM, while 50% growth inhibition was not reached in non-malignant colonic epithelial cells or murine fibroblasts. The compound also reduced clonogenic and CT26 spheroid growth. Treatment induced pronounced vacuolization, accumulation of MDC-positive vesicles, changes in LC3B-II, p62, and ATG5, and reduced FOXM1 abundance, consistent with altered endolysosomal and autophagy-associated processing. DK-AT390HCl achieved measurable systemic exposure. In an orthotopic CT26 model, tumor volume and tumor burden were numerically lower in all treated groups than in untreated controls, but these differences reached statistical significance only for the combination of DK-AT390HCl with 5-fluorouracil after correction for multiple comparisons. These findings identify DK-AT390HCl as a promising starting point for PIKfyve-directed colorectal cancer drug discovery, while further target validation and optimization of cellular potency, solubility, and metabolic stability remain necessary.

articles.title: Combined piperazine ferulate and sulforaphane attenuate methotrexate-induced pulmonary toxicity through modulation of Apelin/APJ, Notch-3, and FOXO3a-associated signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is a widely used chemotherapeutic and immunosuppressive agent; however, its clinical application is frequently limited by the development of pulmonary toxicity. The present study investigated the protective effects of piperazine ferulate (PPZ) and sulforaphane (SFP), administered either individually or in combination, against MTX-induced lung injury, with particular emphasis on oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, autophagy, and their associated signaling pathways. Forty adult male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to five equal groups. Group I served as the normal control, while Groups II-V received a single intraperitoneal injection of MTX (20 mg/kg) on the first day of the experiment to induce pulmonary injury. Rats in Groups III-V were subsequently treated with PPZ (100 mg/kg), SFP (30 mg/kg), or a combination of both agents, respectively, by oral administration once daily for 28 consecutive days. MTX administration induced substantial pulmonary damage, as evidenced by increased oxidative stress, depletion of endogenous antioxidant defenses, including heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and reduced glutathione (GSH), enhanced lipid peroxidation, inflammatory cell infiltration, fibrosis, and increased apoptotic activity. These pathological alterations were accompanied by the upregulation of Apelin, APJ, mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase kinase (MEK), Jagged-1, Notch-3, early growth response-1 (Egr-1), osteopontin (OPN), matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2), and Cyclin D1 expression, together with downregulation of forkhead box O3a (FOXO3a). Furthermore, MTX impaired autophagic activity, as indicated by decreased expression of Beclin-1 and microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3), alongside increased p62 accumulation. Treatment with either PPZ or SFP significantly ameliorated these biochemical, molecular, and histopathological alterations. Notably, the combined administration of PPZ and SFP produced superior protective effects compared with either monotherapy, resulting in marked attenuation of oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, fibrotic remodeling, and apoptotic signaling, while restoring autophagic function and preserving normal pulmonary architecture. PPZ and SFP confer significant protection against MTX-induced pulmonary toxicity, potentially through the modulation of oxidative stress-, inflammation-, apoptosis-, and autophagy-related mechanisms, including the Apelin/APJ, MEK/ERK, Jagged-1/Notch-3, and FOXO3a signaling pathways. Importantly, combined treatment exhibited the greatest protective efficacy, suggesting that this therapeutic strategy may represent a promising adjunctive approach for preventing MTX-associated pulmonary injury.

articles.title: Unique response patterns and high reinforcing efficacy characterize self-administration of combined fentanyl and methamphetamine.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Recent clinical data indicates combined use of fentanyl and methamphetamine (FENT+METH) is climbing, leading to increased adverse health events and deaths. However, preclinical rodent research has not extensively characterized responding and behavioral patterns associated with combined FENT+METH. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to: (1) assess and characterize fixed ratio responding for fentanyl (FENT) alone and in combination with methamphetamine (METH) across sexes; (2) compare the rewarding efficacy of FENT- or METH-alone to that of FENT+METH. METHODS: Male and female Long Evans rats were trained to self-administer FENT, METH, or FENT+METH (2.5 µg/kg/inf FENT, 0.05 mg/kg/inf METH, 2.5 + 0.05 FENT+METH) under long access conditions for fourteen days, followed by ten days of extinction and one day of drug-induced reinstatement. In a separate cohort of animals, progressive ratio responding was used to compare rewarding efficacy between polysubstance and single drug conditions (5 µg/kg/inf FENT, 0.1 mg/kg/inf METH, 5 + 0.1 FENT+METH). RESULTS: Female FENT animals displayed the greatest long access responding, while no differences were observed between drug conditions in males. Across sex, FENT+METH produced distinct response patterns compared to FENT- or METH-alone, producing mostly separate, evenly spaced infusion events, while single drug self-administration produced 'burst-like' responding, with grouped infusions and greater time between infusion events. FENT+METH animals displayed perseverative behavior during extinction, failing to reach extinction criteria. METH-alone engendered the highest responding under drug-induced reinstatement. Under the present experimental doses, FENT+METH had greater reinforcing efficacy than FENT- or METH-alone. CONCLUSIONS: The present findings highlight, across both sexes, the unique response patterns and increased rewarding efficacy produced by FENT+METH self-administration.

articles.title: Integrated evaluation of pharmacokinetics and pharmacogenomics of sunitinib and pazopanib in patients with metastatic renal carcinoma.
articles.abstract: AIM: Sunitinib and pazopanib are anti-angiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) used for metastatic renal cancer, with substantial interindividual variability in drug response. This study aimed to explore factors explaining this variability. METHODS: Pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacogenomics (PG) data from 47 patients enrolled in the SUP-R clinical trial (NCT02555748) were analysed retrospectively (32 treated with sunitinib, 15 with pazopanib). Plasma concentrations measured during the first two treatment cycles were analysed using a non-linear mixed effects model. Exploratory analyses of factors influencing drug exposure, toxicity and efficacy were conducted, including a PG investigation of drug disposition, and target genes and baseline circulating microRNA levels. No correction for multiple comparisons was applied. RESULTS: The PK models adequately described plasma concentration over time in the cohort. Patients experiencing severe toxicity (≥ Grade 3, CTCAE) showed reduced apparent sunitinib clearance (median 24.3 L/h [11.1-45.7] vs. 32.4 L/h [16.6-90.6], p = 0.006). Responders were more exposed to sunitinib and active metabolite SU12662 (observed Ctrough,ss = 140.1 ng/mL [43.2-209.5] vs. 89.5 ng/mL [4.3-230.7], p = 0.036); similar trends were observed with pazopanib, though limited events (3 responders/10 evaluable) precluded definitive interpretation. Carriers of at least one variant ABCB1 c.1199G>A allele were more likely to respond to TKI treatment (odd-ratio = 10.8, 95% confidence interval [1.7-69.9], p = 0.012). CONCLUSION: This study assessed the exposure-response relationships of both drugs and identified potential factors to consider in case of toxicity or treatment failure.

articles.title: Impact of lenvatinib on OATP1B activity in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Lenvatinib (LEN) inhibits organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B1 (OATP1B1) in vitro, raising concern about drug-drug interactions (DDIs). We evaluated the in vivo impact of LEN on OATP1B activity in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), using coproporphyrin-I (CP-I) as endogenous biomarker. METHODS: Twenty-six patients with HCC received LEN in this prospective, single-centre, observational study. Plasma CP-I and total and unbound LEN concentrations were measured at baseline and for 24 h after the first dose. DDI risk was assessed using the ICH M12 basic static model. Changes from baseline were analysed using a linear mixed-effects model on log-transformed concentrations with Dunnett's multiple comparisons and expressed as geometric mean ratios (GMR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: No significant changes in plasma CP-I from baseline were observed at any time point, regardless of OATP1B1 genotype or hepatic function (adjusted p ≥ .25 in all comparisons). Whole-cohort GMRs ranged from 0.97 to 1.11, with upper limit of 95% CI not exceeding 1.30. Baseline CP-I did not differ by genotype (p = .578) but was higher in Child-Pugh B than A (p = .013). Using the basic static model, the median estimated Cmax,inlet,u-to-IC50,u ratio was 0.009, well below the 0.1 threshold. CONCLUSIONS: LEN did not significantly alter OATP1B activity in HCC patients, concordant with static model prediction that first-dose unbound LEN concentrations were far below the threshold for OATP1B1 inhibition. LEN-attributable OATP1B1-mediated DDI risk is therefore low, although this does not account for the reduced baseline OATP1B function inherent to HCC. Caution is warranted when extrapolating these findings to preserved hepatic function.

articles.title: Drug-drug interactions and risk of central nervous system depression in preterm infants: Clinical outcomes from a prospective study.
articles.abstract: AIM: Neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) are frequently exposed to central nervous system (CNS) depressant medications, increasing the risk of potential drug-drug interactions (DDIs). However, evidence on the clinical outcomes associated with these interactions remains limited. This study evaluated the association between DDIs with the potential for CNS depression and clinical outcomes in neonates admitted to a NICU. METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 600 neonates admitted to a NICU in Brazil. Pharmacotherapy was monitored daily, and DDIs with the potential for CNS depression were identified using the UpToDate® database. Clinical outcomes associated with specific drug combinations were analysed. RESULTS: A total of 89 neonates (14.8%) were exposed to at least one DDI with the potential for CNS depression. These interactions were associated with a higher occurrence of hypoactivity, reduced peripheral oxygen saturation and mortality. The fentanyl/phenobarbital combination showed the most consistent risk profile, being associated with all evaluated outcomes. Interactions involving magnesium sulphate were associated with reduced oxygen saturation, while fentanyl/fluconazole was associated with increased mortality. CONCLUSION: DDIs with the potential for CNS depression were associated with clinically relevant adverse outcomes in neonates. The findings highlight fentanyl/phenobarbital as the combination of greatest clinical concern and suggest that oxygen saturation may be a useful marker for monitoring CNS-related DDIs in neonatal intensive care.

articles.title: Simple human pharmacokinetic models scaled-up using cytochrome P450 3A-dependent 6β-hydroxycortisol data from humanized-liver mice can account for monitoring of cortisol administered orally to treat adrenal insufficiency.
articles.abstract: AIM: Endogenous cortisol, a stress biomarker, is used as a cytochrome P450 3A-dependent biomarker for human phenotyping. Because adrenal hypofunction is characterized by low endogenous plasma cortisol levels, exogenous cortisol is therapeutically administered orally in two or three divided daily doses. Simple pharmacokinetic models were established for cortisol monitoring following oral administration. METHODS: One set of model input parameters was based on reported plasma cortisol values in two male Japanese volunteers (designated A and B) orally administered deuterium-labelled cortisol. Simple physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models were also extrapolated from humanized-liver mice data and used to predict human steady-state plasma concentrations of cortisol and its 6β-hydroxylated metabolite. RESULTS: Four groups of humanized-liver mice were used, each with a different human donor. The cortisol clearance values varied by a factor of two across the four groups. This variability was reflected in the in silico clearance values generated as input parameters for PBPK models. Virtual human area-under-the-curve values after oral cortisol (18 mg/day total for 1 week) administered as divided doses once, twice, or thrice daily were used to calculate the mean cortisol and 6β-hydroxycortisol concentrations. For Human A, the mean cortisol level was double that of Human B under the present simulations. CONCLUSIONS: When using 6β-hydroxycortisol as an endogenous biomarker for clinical treatment with exogenous agents, the dosage and timing of oral cortisol should be determined considering individual variations, such as body weight and the twofold variability in baseline normal metabolic enzyme activity.

articles.title: Pop PK-PD model for evaluating the effects of insulin degludec in healthy adult Chinese males.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the dose-response relationship of insulin degludec (IDeg) by linking its pharmacokinetic (PK) exposure to pharmacodynamic (PD) outcomes, supporting evidence-based decision-making in therapeutic development. A single-dose euglycemic clamp study was conducted in 30 healthy adult Chinese male volunteers, from whom 408 plasma samples were collected, yielding a median plasma concentration of 9.57 ng/mL. A population pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (Pop PK-PD model) was developed and validated using Maspectra® software (version 2.8.1) with the first-order conditional estimation with interaction (FOCE-I) method, following a stepwise covariate screening approach. The PK component was best described by a one-compartment model with first-order absorption incorporating an absorption lag time (ALAG) and linear elimination, while the PD component was characterized by a direct-effect Emax model with a Hill coefficient (γ). Body mass index (BMI) significantly influenced the apparent clearance (CL/F), and body weight (BW) significantly affected the apparent volume of distribution (V/F). The final model estimated CL/F = 1.49 L/h, V/F = 25.3 L, absorption rate constant (ka) = 0.10 h-1, ALAG = 0.72 h, maximum effect (Emax) = 3.70 mg/kg/min, half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) = 15.35 ng/mL, and γ = 4.13. Comprehensive model evaluation using goodness-of-fit plots, bootstrap analysis, and visual predictive check (VPC) confirmed that the model exhibits good stability, accurate parameter estimates, and reliable predictive performance. In conclusion, a robust and reliable Pop PK-PD model based on a one-compartment structure with direct effect was successfully developed in healthy adult males, providing a useful simulation foundation for subsequent insulin-related clinical trials in similar populations. Nevertheless, dedicated external validation studies in broader, more clinically representative cohorts, including female subjects and patients with diabetes across different disease stages, are strictly warranted before the model can be confidently extended to support general clinical dose selection and routine therapeutic decision-making. This study was registered on the Drug Clinical Trial Registration and Information Disclosure Platform, registration number: CTR20201129, registration date: June 5, 2020.

articles.title: Oroxylin A attenuates pneumonia via HSP90α-dependent suppression of macrophage ferroptosis-mediated inflammation.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the protective activity of Oroxylin A in pneumonia and to clarify the mechanisms involved, particularly those associated with macrophage-driven inflammation and ferroptosis. Pneumonia was induced in mice and treated with Oroxylin A, followed by evaluation of lung injury, inflammatory cytokine production, and ferroptosis-related markers. Pulmonary immune alterations were further characterized by single-cell RNA sequencing. Target-responsive accessibility profiling, molecular dynamics simulation, and cellular thermal shift assays were subsequently applied to explore potential molecular targets, followed by functional verification in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-challenged macrophages. Oroxylin A alleviated body weight loss, pathological lung injury, alveolar inflammation, and inflammatory cytokine production in mice with pneumonia. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis identified macrophages as a major responsive population and showed that Oroxylin A modulated inflammation- and ferroptosis-related transcriptional programs. In LPS-stimulated macrophages, Oroxylin A suppressed the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and increased GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression, whereas these effects were attenuated by erastin. Heat shock protein 90-alpha (HSP90α) was further identified as a potential binding target of Oroxylin A. In silico perturbation analyses suggested that HSP90α participates in ferroptosis-related biological processes. Functional experiments showed that HSP90α overexpression weakened the anti-inflammatory and anti-ferroptotic actions of Oroxylin A, whereas HSP90α knockdown suppressed inflammatory cytokine expression and increased GPX4 expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that Oroxylin A alleviates pneumonia-associated inflammation through an HSP90α-dependent mechanism involving the regulation of macrophage ferroptosis.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics and prophylactic detoxifying efficacy of CocH5-Fc(M6) against cocaethylene and norcocaethylene in male rats.
articles.abstract: Concurrent consumption of cocaine and alcohol generates the more toxic cocaine metabolites cocaethylene and norcocaethylene, increasing neurotoxicity, cardiotoxicity, and mortality risk. Traditional therapeutic interventions fail to address this complex polysubstance profile. This study evaluates the in vivo prophylactic efficacy of CocH5-Fc(M6), an engineered highly effective long-acting cocaine hydrolase, against these toxic, exogenously administered alcohol-derived metabolites. In vitro kinetic analysis demonstrated that CocH5-Fc(M6) exhibits high catalytic efficiency against cocaethylene (1.55 × 109 min-1M-1) and hydrolysis-resistant norcocaethylene (6.11 × 107 min-1M-1), resulting in a 3,500-fold and a 75-fold enhancement over the wild-type butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), respectively. In a male rat model, intravenous administration of 1 mg/kg CocH5-Fc(M6) given 1 min prior to challenge completely prevented acute mortality against a lethal dose (LD100) of exogenous cocaethylene (125 mg/kg, i.p.). Pharmacokinetic monitoring revealed that the cocaine hydrolase substantially suppressed systemic parent drug levels to 327 ± 427 nM within 5 min and to baseline by 30 min. This rapid clearance was driven by highly efficient metabolic shunting that also markedly reduced substrate availability for oxidative metabolism. Consequently, systemic levels of toxic norcocaethylene were restricted to 73.5 ± 25.0 nM, while the benign cleavage metabolite, ecgonine ethyl ester, surged to 27,254 ± 7,595 nM. Plasma monitoring verified that the enzyme maintained stable, long-circulating concentrations (>10 mg/L) across the 180-minute testing window. These findings demonstrate that CocH5-Fc(M6) effectively neutralized cocaethylene-induced lethality in vivo, highlighting its translational potential for protective intervention against toxic metabolites from cocaine-alcohol polydrug use.

articles.title: Evaluation of enteric polymer-based amorphous solid dispersions performance during pH-shift dissolution: insights for weakly acidic drugs.
articles.abstract: Amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) formulated with enteric polymers are increasingly employed to improve the oral delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs. However, mechanistic investigations of their performance during gastrointestinal pH transitions (two- or three- stage dissolution studies) have focused predominantly on weakly basic compounds, leaving the behavior of weakly acidic active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) insufficiently understood. This study therefore sought to investigate the pH-shift dissolution behavior of weakly acidic APIs, using indomethacin (IND) as a model drug, in ASDs prepared with hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate (HPMCAS) and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose phthalate (HPMCP). Polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) was also included as a non-enteric reference polymer for comparison. ASDs containing 25% and 40% (w/w) IND were prepared by melt-quench cooling and evaluated under one-stage intestinal conditions (pH6.8) and two-stage pH-shift conditions (pH1.6 → 6.8 and pH5.0 → 6.8), representing fasted- and fed-state gastric environments, respectively, before transition to intestinal conditions. Under one-stage intestinal conditions, PVP-based ASDs exhibited the highest dissolution performance, whereas the enteric polymers HPMCAS and HPMCP provided greater resistance to hydration-induced crystallization. During pH-shift dissolution, HPMCAS uniquely preserved its dissolution performance following exposure to pH5.0 (AUC ratio 1.04-1.05), while all other formulations exhibited reduced performance (AUC ratios 0.84-0.93). This behavior was accompanied by comparatively stable colloidal populations in HPMCAS-based ASDs, whereas solution-state 1H NMR revealed polymer-dependent molecular organization that did not directly correlate with dissolution or crystallization behavior. In contrast to previous studies on weakly basic drugs, where hydration-induced surface crystallization was identified as the primary factor governing subsequent intestinal drug release, the present systems exhibited a different physicochemical behavior, characterized by polymer-dependent molecular organization and colloidal evolution in the absence of detectable hydration-induced crystallization.

articles.title: Extracellular matrix hydrogel modified by miR-21-overexpressing keratinocyte-derived exosomes accelerates burn wound healing.
articles.abstract: Skin wound healing involves a complex interplay among various cell types. Extracellular matrix (ECM) hydrogels are promising candidates for tissue repair because of their biocompatibility and biomimetic architecture; however, they lack sufficient bioactive signals to actively promote healing. MicroRNA-21 (miR-21) is a crucial regulator of wound repair, and exosomes can serve as effective vehicles for delivering miR-21 to target cells. In this study, we developed an injectable thermosensitive composite system (ECM@Exo-miR-21) by incorporating keratinocyte-derived exosomes enriched with miR-21 into an ECM hydrogel. In vitro results demonstrated that ECM@Exo-miR-21 significantly enhanced the functions of human dermal fibroblasts, keratinocytes, and umbilical vein endothelial cells. In a murine model of deep second-degree burns, ECM@Exo-miR-21 markedly expedited wound closure. Histological evaluations revealed improved re-epithelialization, increased collagen deposition, enhanced neovascularization, and an attenuated inflammatory response. Collectively, ECM@Exo-miR-21 integrates keratinocyte-derived exosomes rich in miR-21 with a biomimetic ECM microenvironment to prolong the local retention time of the composite formulation, thereby comprehensively facilitating burn wound healing. The favorable therapeutic outcomes are attributed to the composite formulation, while the specific contribution of miR-21 enrichment warrants further investigation. This approach provides a novel strategy for developing functional materials for wound repair.

articles.title: Development of follicle-targeted polymeric emulsions to enhance topical delivery of a curcumin-derived AR degrader for acne therapy.
articles.abstract: Acne vulgaris is driven in part by androgen receptor (AR) signaling in the sebaceous gland, and topical AR blockade with clascoterone, the first approved topical AR inhibitor for acne, has validated this pathway clinically. AR degradation offers an alternative that removes the receptor rather than occupying it. MI131 is a curcumin-derived AR degrader disclosed in CN116969828B. Here, a polymer-stabilized emulsion was developed to deliver MI131 to the pilosebaceous unit. After optimization of the emulsifier system, emulsions containing 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5% (w/w) MI131 were characterized for droplet size, rheology, in vitro release and physical stability. Droplets were spherical and submicron in size, with median diameters (D50) of 0.89-0.94 µm across the three loadings. The emulsions showed shear-thinning behavior, released MI131 by Higuchi-type diffusion and remained physically stable over the study period. After topical application in Bama minipigs, MI131 accumulated in the epidermis and dermis with low systemic exposure, and deposition in follicular skin exceeded that in non-follicular skin. In the Syrian hamster flank-organ model, the polymeric emulsion suppressed androgen-driven enlargement of the sebaceous gland, with the 0.5% formulation showing the largest effect. AR protein in the sebaceous glands decreased, consistent with degradation rather than receptor blockade. These results show that a polymer-stabilized emulsion delivers MI131 to the sebaceous gland and supports topical AR degradation as a strategy for acne treatment.

articles.title: Electrochemically assisted controlled-release study of the anticancer drug 5-fluorouracil by using fabrication of skin-simulating chip as a transdermal drug delivery model.
articles.abstract: The controlled release of cancer drugs is vital for minimizing side effects and ensuring the desired therapeutic outcomes. In this study, we developed conductive polymer coated on carbon felt (CF) as a soft pad to investigate the controlled-release of the anticancer drug 5-fluorouracil. This process utilizes the electrical properties of the conductive polymer, polypyrrole (PPy) which also responds to changes in pH. By applying various electrical potentials at different pH levels and temperatures, the pad can release different amounts of the drug over time. The drug release profile was continuously monitored in real time through a combination of spectrometry and electrochemical methods. The findings indicated that increasing the applied electrical potential significantly accelerated the rate of drug release. The release rate constants were obtained by fitting the data with the Avrami equation, while the activation parameters were determined using the Arrhenius and Eyring equations. This designed system allows for control of drug release from the prepared soft pad at a low potential of -0.6 V, making it ideal for clinical applications, particularly in transdermal delivery. Given that the 5-fluorouracil is an anti-skin cancer drug, a skin-simulating chip was design and fabricate to investigate its release and transdermal delivery. The findings confirmed the effectiveness of the soft pads in facilitating controlled drug release and delivery in different potentials.

articles.title: PFI-3 attenuates atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability and modulates a BRG1-SLUG-miR-193b-3p-CD47 axis in cultured vascular smooth muscle cells.
articles.abstract: AIMS: CD47, a "don't-eat-me" signal overexpressed in atherosclerotic lesions, impairs efferocytosis and promotes plaque instability. BRG1 (SMARCA4), the catalytic ATPase of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complex, drives vascular inflammation, yet its role in CD47 regulation remains unknown. We investigated whether PFI-3, an inhibitor of the BRG1/SMARCA4, BRM/SMARCA2, and PBRM1 bromodomains, attenuates plaque vulnerability and delineated the BRG1-dependent cascade regulating CD47 in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). MATERIALS AND METHODS: High-fat-diet-fed ApoE-/- mice received oral PFI-3 or vehicle; plaque burden, composition, and efferocytosis were assessed histologically. LPS-stimulated mouse VSMCs (mVSMCs) underwent BRG1 knockdown or PFI-3 treatment followed by macrophage engulfment assays. ChIP-qPCR, dual-luciferase, and epistatic rescue experiments defined the regulatory cascade. KEY FINDINGS: PFI-3 reduced plaque area, necrotic core size, and macrophage infiltration while increasing collagen and α-SMA content, without altering circulating lipids. Free apoptotic cells decreased and macrophage-associated clearance increased. In vitro, LPS co-upregulated BRG1, SLUG, and CD47 in mVSMCs. BRG1 silencing suppressed SLUG and CD47 and enhanced phagocytosis. ChIP confirmed BRG1 occupancy at the SLUG promoter; SLUG repressed miR-193b-3p, which targeted the CD47 3'-UTR. PFI-3 phenocopied BRG1 knockdown by restoring miR-193b-3p and suppressing CD47. SIGNIFICANCE: This study identifies a BRG1 → SLUG→miR-193b-3p → CD47 cascade in mVSMCs whereby BRG1 elevates CD47 under inflammation to impair efferocytosis. PFI-3 suppresses this axis in vitro and attenuates plaque vulnerability in vivo - although contributions from BRM/SMARCA2 and PBRM1 inhibition cannot be excluded. These findings support further investigation of PFI-3 and this regulatory axis in atherosclerosis.

articles.title: SH2B1 modulates hepatic lipid droplet homeostasis and is associated with HSC70/LAMP2A-related PLIN2 regulation in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease.
articles.abstract: AIMS: SH2B adaptor protein 1 (SH2B1) participates in metabolic regulation, but its role in hepatic lipid-droplet homeostasis remains unclear. We investigated its role and underlying mechanisms in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Human and mouse GEO transcriptomic datasets and liver single-cell RNA-sequencing data were analyzed to characterize SH2B1 expression and identify lipid-metabolism-related candidates. SH2B1 knockdown and overexpression were performed in palmitate/oleate (P/O)-treated AML12 hepatocytes, and lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 A (LAMP2A) knockdown was combined with SH2B1 overexpression to assess its functional contribution. Molecular docking explored potential interactions, while reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence assessed protein association and colocalization, respectively. In vivo, mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) and subsequently underwent AAV-mediated hepatic Sh2b1 knockdown. KEY FINDINGS: SH2B1 expression was reduced in human and murine fatty liver datasets and was predominantly detected in hepatocytes. Perilipin 2 (PLIN2) expression was inversely correlated with SH2B1 across GSE165855 samples. P/O exposure reduced SH2B1 expression and increased PLIN2 levels and lipid accumulation. SH2B1 knockdown increased PLIN2 abundance and lipid storage, whereas overexpression produced the opposite phenotype. Reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation supported an association between SH2B1 and heat shock cognate 70 (HSC70), and immunofluorescence demonstrated their colocalization. SH2B1 manipulation bidirectionally altered LAMP2A abundance. LAMP2A knockdown attenuated the reductions in PLIN2 abundance and lipid accumulation induced by SH2B1 overexpression. Hepatic Sh2b1 knockdown exacerbated HFD-induced hepatic lipid accumulation and liver injury, with lower LAMP2A and higher PLIN2 levels. SIGNIFICANCE: SH2B1 regulates hepatic lipid-droplet homeostasis, with LAMP2A contributing to its effects on PLIN2 abundance and lipid accumulation.

articles.title: Ampelopsis grossedentata restores the homeostasis of Th17/Treg cells to mitigate DSS-induced ulcerative colitis through TLR1-2/NF-κB signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ampelopsis grossedentata (AG), a traditional medicine from Southwest China, is frequently used to treat inflammation, anemopyretic cold, pharyngitis, hepatitis, and dysentery. Pharmacological studies confirmed that primary active constituents of AG, including flavonoids, profoundly affect anti-inflammatory processes and immunomodulation. However, the therapeutic effect and mechanisms of AG for ulcerative colitis (UC) are still unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to elucidate the mechanisms of AG treatment of UC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: UPLC-MS and network pharmacology were employed to identify the active components of AG and their potential anti-UC mechanisms. A 4% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced UC mouse model was established for assessing therapeutic efficacy of AG based on body weight, disease activity index, colon length, and histopathology of colon tissue. RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence assays and D-lactate levels were used to evaluate the inflammatory state and epithelial barrier integrity. Transcriptomic, proteomic, and flow cytometry analyses were performed to examine the underlying mechanisms. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), western blot and the TLR1/2 knockdown assays were used to identify and verify candidate targets. RESULTS: Five flavonoids in AG were characterized via UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, with dihydromyricetin, taxifolin, myricitrin, and myricetin quantified by HPLC-DAD. Network pharmacology revealed 38 UC-related targets, enriched in IL-17/TNF signaling pathways. In vivo, AG alleviated UC-related symptoms, improved colon pathology, reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6), upregulated tight junction proteins (ZO-1, claudin 5), and inhibited the nuclear translocation of NF-κB (P65 and P50). Transcriptomic, proteomic, and flow cytometry analyses indicated that AG regulated Th17/Treg balance via the NF-κB signaling pathway. Structure-based molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, CETSA western blot and the TLR1/2 knockdown assays revealed that AG may act through the TLR1-TLR2 heterodimer receptor. CONCLUSION: AG effectively attenuates DSS-induced UC, potentially by restoring Th17/Treg balance and inhibiting NF-κB signaling through the TLR1-TLR2 heterodimer. AG is thus a therapeutic candidate for UC treatment.

articles.title: Case Report: Raw grass carp gallbladder ingestion and acute liver injury.
articles.abstract: Raw grass carp gallbladder ingestion for folk medicinal purposes may cause severe acute liver injury driven by the hepatotoxin 5α-cyprinol sulfate, yet high-dose human poisoning cases remain infrequently documented. We report a 60-year-old male (60 kg body weight) who developed severe intoxication 22 h after consuming six raw gallbladders from grass carps of approximately 1.5 kg each. Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and watery diarrhoea occurred within 2 hours of ingestion. Laboratory testing on admission demonstrated extreme hepatocellular injury (ALT 6285 U/L, AST 9321 U/L). Conventional hepatoprotective agents plus pre-hospital haemoperfusion yielded limited biochemical improvement. While admitted to the intensive care unit, the patient received one session of double plasma molecular adsorption system, three sessions of plasma exchange and four sessions of continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT, CVVHDF modality) alongside comprehensive supportive care. Liver function normalized within 14 hospital days; no acute kidney injury was observed. Complete symptomatic recovery was documented at the 4-week follow-up visit, though longer-term outcomes remain unknown given the limited follow-up duration. Toxin-mediated hepatocyte damage is partially supported by pre-clinical cyprinol-sulfate experimental work; many downstream oxidative, mitochondrial, endoplasmic-reticulum and inflammatory molecular pathways remain hypothetical and are largely extrapolated from unrelated liver-injury models, without direct validation in human carp-gallbladder-poisoning tissue specimens. Biochemical improvement was temporally associated with multimodal extracorporeal purification, but causal therapeutic benefit can't be proven from this uncontrolled single case; spontaneous hepatic regeneration may also contribute to recovery. This case highlights substantial hazards associated with folk-health beliefs promoting raw fish-gallbladder consumption, emphasising the need for early clinical recognition of fish-gallbladder poisoning.

articles.title: Enhancing the antidepressant effects of scopolamine through mGlu2 receptor antagonism as an emerging approach for treating depression.
articles.abstract: Conventional antidepressants remain not effective enough to treat depression, with only 30-40% of patients achieving full remission. This has intensified the call for a deeper understanding of depression's biological mechanisms, moving beyond the traditional monoaminergic hypothesis. The cholinergic hypothesis, first proposed in the 1970s, has gained renewed interest due to the rapid antidepressant effects of scopolamine, a muscarinic receptor antagonist. Despite its potential, scopolamine's side effects hinder clinical use. Recent research highlights dysregulation of glutamatergic neurotransmission in depression, and targeting metabotropic glutamate (mGlu) receptors presents a novel therapeutic strategy. Evidence suggests that mGlu2 receptors play a critical role in the rapid antidepressant effect, and mGlu2 receptor antagonists possess antidepressant-like potential in animal models of depression. Importantly, mGlu2 antagonists such as LY341495 or the mGlu2 negative allosteric modulator VU6001966, when coadministered with scopolamine, enhance scopolamine's antidepressant efficacy while reducing cognitive side effects. Data indicate that ligands of other mGlu receptor subtypes, including group III mGlu receptors, may also enhance the therapeutic effects of scopolamine while avoiding undesirable effects. This review study underscores the urgent need for innovative approaches to depression treatment, emphasizing the importance of mGlu2 as a promising target for future therapeutic development, especially as co-treatment with low doses of scopolamine. The mechanism related to the potentiation of the antidepressant effect of scopolamine by VU6001966, including activation of AMPA receptors and BDNF-TrkB signaling, is also discussed.

articles.title: Rifampicin and long-acting cabotegravir-rilpivirine: Therapeutic drug monitoring-guided management of a major drug-drug interaction-A case report.
articles.abstract: Long-acting injectable cabotegravir/rilpivirine (LAI CAB/RPV) is subject to clinically significant drug-drug interactions with strong enzyme inducers such as rifampicin due to markedly reduced drug exposure and potential development of resistance. However, real-world evidence on managing this interaction remains scarce. We report a person with HIV, virologically suppressed on LAI CAB/RPV, who developed an orthopaedic implant-associated infection requiring 10-week rifampicin-containing therapy for its antibiofilm activity. Further LAI CAB/RPV injections were withheld, and oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine once daily plus dolutegravir 50 mg twice daily was initiated. This regimen was continued until 3 weeks after rifampicin discontinuation; afterwards, dolutegravir was reduced to once daily. LAI CAB/RPV was restarted 5 weeks after rifampicin withdrawal; oral antiretroviral therapy was discontinued. Serial therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) showed a rapid decline in plasma CAB and RPV concentrations from day 8 after rifampicin initiation, with both drugs falling below the efficacy thresholds by day 10.
