In contrast, tenofovir and dolutegravir concentrations remained within the therapeutic range during rifampicin co-administration, whereas twice-daily dolutegravir concentrations exceeded the therapeutic range 3 weeks after rifampicin discontinuation. HIV RNA remained undetectable throughout follow-up. This case confirms the clinically relevant interaction between rifampicin and LAI CAB/RPV, as illustrated by the rapid decline in residual CAB and RPV plasma concentrations following rifampicin initiation. Temporary substitution with a recommended first-line oral antiretroviral regimen maintained adequate drug exposure, was well tolerated and preserved virological suppression throughout rifampicin treatment. TDM allowed to characterize the interaction and may support individualized management in selected complex clinical situations.

articles.title: The Inhibition of Biotransformation Enzymes Affects the Response of PC3 Prostate Cancer Cell Line to Docetaxel.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Targeting drug-metabolizing enzymes in tumor cells may improve chemoprevention and chemotherapy by providing new targets for anticancer agents or combination therapies. This study investigated whether inhibition of CYP1A1, CYP3A4, and GSTP1 by α-naphthoflavone, ketoconazole, and quercetin modulates docetaxel activity in PC3 prostate cancer cells and PNT1A prostate epithelial cells. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PC3 and PNT1A cells were exposed to docetaxel either alone or in combination with inhibitors of CYP1A1, CYP3A4, and GSTP1. Sub-lethal monotherapy doses were calibrated to produce approximately 70% cell viability at 24 hours and 60% at 48 hours. Cell viability was assessed by WST-1 assay, while apoptosis and necrosis were evaluated using Annexin V staining. Enzyme activities were measured by ELSA. Cellular oxidative activity was assessed by DCFDA fluorescence analysis. RESULTS: In PC3 cells, calibrated monotherapy doses were: 4 µM docetaxel, 1000 nM α-naphthoflavone, 56.5 µM ketoconazole, and 300 µM quercetin. Combination treatments reduced cell viability by an additional 12-25% at 24 hours and by up to 45% at 48 hours, compared with docetaxel alone. Docetaxel treatment induced time-dependent changes in enzyme activities, whereas combination treatments markedly reduced DCFDA fluorescence signals. CONCLUSION: Co-administration of docetaxel with CYP1A1, CYP3A4, and GSTP1-related pharmacological modulators may enhance cytotoxicity in prostate cancer cells. Increased cytotoxicity was accompanied by reduced DCFDA fluorescence, indicating that enhanced treatment responses were not necessarily associated with increased oxidative fluorescence signals.

articles.title: Prevalence and Characteristics of Potential QT-Interval-Prolonging Drug-Drug Interactions in Patients Receiving Oral Anticancer Drugs.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with cancer are at increased risk of QT interval prolongation because of polypharmacy and concomitant use of QT-prolonging medications. Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) may further increase this risk. Outpatient electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring appears to be underused among patients receiving oral anticancer drugs (OADs). Our study objective was to evaluate the prevalence and characteristics of potential QT interval-prolonging drug-drug interactions (QT pDDIs) in patients with cancer receiving OAD therapy. METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted using electronic health record data from 3697 patients with advanced cancer. Patients who received at least one OAD were included in the analysis. Potential QT-related DDIs were identified through overlap prescriptions of concomitant medications associated with QT prolongation and/or Cytochrome P450- (CYP-) or drug transporter-mediated interactions during OAD exposure. Descriptive analyses were performed to characterize the prevalence and types of QT pDDIs. RESULTS: Of the 3697 patients, 1732 (46.8%) received at least one OAD and were included in the analysis. Of these, 17.1% experienced at least one QT pDDI. Among those patients, 47.5% experienced PD-QT pDDIs only, 21.2% experienced PK-QT pDDIs only, and 31.3% experienced both PD- and PK-QT pDDIs during OAD exposure. Concurrent PD and PK mechanisms occurred simultaneously in 30.6% of patients with QT-pDDIs. Approximately 48% of identified QT pDDIs involved at least one OAD, most commonly pazopanib (13.5%), palbociclib (11.3%), and vandetanib (8.4%). CONCLUSION: QT pDDIs were common among patients with cancer receiving OADs, highlighting the importance of comprehensive DDI screening, careful medication review, and enhanced cardiac monitoring strategies in oncology practice.
